content: # Thinking with Computational Models: companion app # One investigation in seven steps, following Sections 2 to 8 of the paper. The # reader works out what one learning rule implies, finds a comparison in which # two explanations of blocking disagree, examines what the disagreement depends # on, asks how it would appear in responses, analyzes a simulated experiment, # checks a prediction that all its candidates share, and sees two settings of a # model of simple decisions that only a different measurement can tell apart. # Explore lets the reader change the settings freely. # # Files in R/ are loaded by Shiny before this one: # models.R the learning models (a copy of R/models.R; the tests require # the two to be identical) # engine.R the model calculations, except the experiments of Steps 5 # and 6; checked by tests/verify_app.R # formulas.R displayed model equations and their symbols # helpers.R shared text, number formats and small building blocks # ask.R questions, saved answers, and notes # plots.R figures # opening.R the opening and the step buttons # rule.R Step 1, Section 2 # explanations.R Step 2, Section 3 # assumptions.R Step 3, Section 4 # behavior.R Step 4, Section 5 # experiment.R Step 5, Section 6 (responses from data/inference_cases.rds, # written by shiny_app/make_inference_cases.R) # shared.R Step 6, Section 7 # measurement.R Step 7, Section 8 # explore.R the Explore tab # values.R the model results the page shows, computed once at startup # tests/verify_app_flow.R walks through the seven steps, and # tests/verify_app_feedback.R checks the feedback on every combination of answers. # # Requirements: shiny, bslib, ggplot2 # Launch from the repository root: shiny::runApp("shiny_app") library(shiny) library(bslib) library(ggplot2) # UI # The steps with the notes beside them. On narrow screens the notes come after # the steps, and a small fixed link jumps there. with_notes <- function(content) div(class = "layout", div(class = "main part", content), div(class = "notes", id = "notes_box", tags$details(id = "notes_details", open = NA, tags$summary(h2("Your notes")), downloadLink("notes_download", "Download notes (.txt)"), uiOutput("notes"))), tags$a(class = "notes-jump", href = "#notes_box", "Notes")) about <- div(class = "part", h2(class = "about", "About this page"), p(HTML("You can work through this page without reading the accompanying tutorial, Thinking with Computational Models to Guide Scientific Inquiry by Kenny Yu (KU Leuven). Both use the same learning task and the same two learning models, Rescorla–Wagner and the adaptive model, followed by a model of simple decisions. The seven steps follow Sections 2 to 8 of the tutorial.")), p("For the derivations, the code checks and the full simulation study, follow the references marked “In the tutorial” or inspect the R scripts in the repository linked below."), h3("Where the numbers come from"), p("Steps 1 to 4 and Explore calculate the model predictions as you use the page. Step 7 calculates accuracy and decision times from the drift diffusion model. The numerical checks compare these results with the tutorial."), p("Steps 5 and 6 use saved simulated experiments from the tutorial's study. Changing the sample size or the analyzed pear trials selects the corresponding responses and analysis. The page does not fit any models while you use it."), p("The saved cases use the base parameter set. The percentages shown with them summarize 400 experiments for each process and design, 100 under each of four parameter sets."), tags$details(class = "formula-details", tags$summary("Code and numerical checks"), P("The learning calculations use shiny_app/R/models.R, an identical copy of R/models.R used in the tutorial. The engine of the page is shiny_app/R/engine.R. tests/verify_app.R checks both against the reported values, including the light's learned value of ", num(rw_tr$V_B_after[20], 4), " after ten compound trials under ", RW, " and the adaptive model's B–D gap of ", num(at(base$adaptive$gap, 8)), " after eight pear trials."), P("For Steps 5 and 6, shiny_app/make_inference_cases.R regenerates one experiment of each size per generating process from saved random seeds. It analyzes every design with the study's code and stops if a result disagrees with the corresponding saved analysis of the study.")), p(HTML(paste0("Code and materials: ", "github.com/kennychechuanyu/thinking_with_simulations."))) ) ui <- page_fixed( theme = bs_theme(version = 5, bg = "#FFFFFF", fg = "#252525", primary = "#252525", base_font = font_collection("Charter", "Georgia", "Cambria", "serif"), heading_font = font_collection("Charter", "Georgia", "serif")), title = "Thinking with Computational Models", tags$head(tags$link(rel = "stylesheet", href = "style.css"), tags$script(src = "scenes.js"), tags$script(HTML(" document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('scroll_top', function (m) { var heading = document.querySelector('.opening'); if (heading) { heading.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1'); heading.focus({ preventScroll: true }); } window.scrollTo(0, 0); }); });"))), div(class = "masthead", h1("Thinking with Computational Models"), p("One investigation, worked through in seven steps.")), navset_underline(id = "tabs", nav_panel("The inquiry", with_notes(tagList(opening_ui(), rule_ui(), explanations_ui(), assumptions_ui(), behavior_ui(), experiment_ui(), shared_ui(), measurement_ui()))), nav_panel("Explore", explore_ui()), nav_panel("About", about)) ) # Server server <- function(input, output, session) { # The saved answer to each question, and the entries of the notes. answers <- reactiveValues() entries <- reactiveVal(list()) add_note <- function(...) entries(c(entries(), list(note(...)))) # A logical output read by conditionalPanel. The "..." lets both Shiny and # shiny::testServer call it. The flags that complete Steps 1 to 7 also go # to scenes.js, which marks the step complete. step_flags <- c("done_q1c", "done_q2d", "done_q3e", "done_q4c", "done_e4", "done_f5", "done_x3") flag <- function(name, condition) { output[[name]] <- function(...) condition() outputOptions(output, name, suspendWhenHidden = FALSE) if (name %in% step_flags) observe(session$sendCustomMessage("scene_done", list(name = name, done = isTRUE(condition())))) } # One flag per question, done_q1a and so on: TRUE once it has been answered. for (id in c("q1a", "q1b", "q1c", "q2a", "q2b", "q2c", "q2d", "q3a", "q3b", "q3c", "q3d", "q3e", "q4a", "q4b", "q4c", "e_design", "e1", "e2", "e3", "e4", "f1", "f2", "f3", "f4", "f5", "x1", "x2", "x3")) local({ i <- id; flag(paste0("done_", i), function() !is.null(answers[[i]])) }) output$notes <- renderUI(notes_ui(entries())) output$notes_download <- downloadHandler( filename = function() paste0("thinking-with-models-notes-", Sys.Date(), ".txt"), content = function(file) writeLines(notes_text(entries()), file)) rule <- rule_server(input, output, answers, add_note) explanations <- explanations_server(input, output, answers, add_note) assumptions <- assumptions_server(input, output, answers, add_note) behavior <- behavior_server(input, output, answers, add_note) experiment <- experiment_server(input, output, answers, add_note, flag) shared <- shared_server(input, output, answers, add_note, flag, experiment) measurement <- measurement_server(input, output, answers, add_note) explore <- explore_server(input, output, session) # Trying another case or design clears the answers of Steps 5 to 7, since # Step 6 opens only after Step 5 and Step 7 only after Step 6. The notes are # kept. observeEvent(input$e_again, { experiment$reset(); shared$reset(); measurement$reset() }) # Starting again clears the answers of every step and keeps the notes. observeEvent(input$restart, { rule$reset(); explanations$reset(); assumptions$reset(); behavior$reset() experiment$reset(); shared$reset(); measurement$reset() session$sendCustomMessage("scroll_top", TRUE) }) } shinyApp(ui, server)

# Step 3: what the disagreement depends on (Section 4)
# The interventions Prevent, Remove and Supply; the carryover of associability
# and of learned value, with the reader's conclusion before and after (Box 3);
# the amount of training and the rate eta; and the rule for associability.

assumptions_ui <- function() {
  scene("scene-3", "3", "What the disagreement depends on", "output.done_q2d", "done_q3e",
    "With no carried-over learned value, removing the associability difference removes the gap. Carried-over learned value gives Rescorla–Wagner a gap too, largest before the first pear trial. Under a rank-based rule, a tiny salience difference removes most of the gap, and if ties also lower associability there is no gap at all.",
    P("Under ", RW, ", ", B_gloss, " and ", D_gloss, " learned identically about the pear,
       whereas under the adaptive model D pulled ahead, because B brought a lower learning rate
       into the pear trials. This step changes the choices behind that result. In the terms of
       the opening, what carries over, the amount of training and the rate η at which
       associability changes are settings. The rule for associability is one of the model's
       rules."),
    h3("Checking the explanation by changing the model"),
    p("We attributed the adaptive model's gap to B's lower associability. To check that
       explanation, we change the choice we believe produced the result and see what happens.
       In an experiment we cannot set a participant's associability, but in a simulation we
       can. The tutorial calls these three interventions Prevent, Remove and Supply. In all
       three, learned values for the apple do not carry over to the pear trials."),
    tags$ul(
      tags$li("Prevent: hold every cue's associability fixed during the compound trials, while
               learned values change as usual. B and D both keep their starting associability of
               .5. From the first pear trial on, associability changes as usual again."),
      tags$li(HTML(paste0("Remove: let associability change as usual during the compound
               trials, so B's falls to about ", num(trained$adaptive$alpha_B), ", then reset B's
               and D's associabilities to .5 before the pear trials."))),
      tags$li(HTML(paste0("Supply: give a ", RW, " learner the learning rates with which the
               adaptive model starts the pear trials, about ", num(trained$adaptive$rate_B),
               " for B and ", num(trained$adaptive$rate_D), " for D, and keep them fixed. Each
               light is trained alone with the pear, so its shared error is its own error, as in
               the adaptive model. Supply and the adaptive model differ only in whether the
               learning rates change.")))),
    div(class = "question", uiOutput("q3a")),
    conditionalPanel("output.done_q3a",
      fig("p3_runs", "300px"),
      h3("What carries over to the new outcome"),
      p("So far the lights' learned values for the apple did not carry over to the pear trials,
         whereas the associability they acquired carried over in full. Earlier training could
         affect the pear trials in two ways. It could change how much the lights learn from a
         given error, or how much they already predict when the pear trials begin. The two can
         occur together, so each has its own fraction."),
      P("First consider associability. Suppose that only a fraction ", gA, " of the change in
         associability during the compound trials carries over. With ", gA, " = 1, as in Step 2,
         B begins the pear trials with associability about ", num(trained$adaptive$alpha_B),
         " and D with ", num(trained$adaptive$alpha_D), ". With half carryover, B begins with
         about ", num(ga_half$start$alpha_B), ", and with none, both begin with .5. The fraction
         applies to the change in associability, not to associability itself. Both lights start
         the pear trials at zero and share the salience .3, so each gains .3 times its starting
         associability on its first pear trial. Half carryover therefore halves the gap after
         that trial, from about ", num(at(base$adaptive$gap, 1)), " to ",
         num(at(ga_half$adaptive$gap, 1)), ". How much associability people carry over is an
         empirical question."),
      tags$details(class = "worked-example",
        tags$summary(HTML(paste0("Try other values of ", gA))),
        sliderInput("ga", HTML(paste0("Carryover of associability, ", gA)),
                    min = 0, max = 1, value = .5, step = .05, ticks = FALSE, width = "320px"),
        uiOutput("ga_text"),
        fig("p3_ga", "280px")),
      P("Now suppose that some of what each light learned about the apple also enters its first
         prediction about the pear. A second fraction, ", gV, ", sets each light's starting value
         for the pear to ", gV, " times its learned value for the apple. With ", gV, " = 0, both
         lights start the pear trials at zero, as in Step 2. With ", gV, " = 1, each starts with
         its full value for the apple. Within each model, the same fraction applies to both
         lights."),
      carryover_formulas_ui(),
      div(class = "question", uiOutput("q3b"))),
    conditionalPanel("output.done_q3b",
      div(class = "question", uiOutput("q3c"))),
    conditionalPanel("output.done_q3c",
      P("Try a few values of ", gV, ". Both models use the same value, and the adaptive model
         keeps all of its change in associability. Look at the gap before the first pear trial
         as well as the gap during the pear trials."),
      sliderInput("gv", HTML(paste0("Carryover of learned value, ", gV)),
                  min = 0, max = 1, value = .5, step = .05, ticks = FALSE, width = "320px"),
      uiOutput("gv_text"),
      fig("p3_gap", "280px"),
      fig("p3_grid", "280px"),
      P("As more of the value for the apple carries over, the ", RW, " gap grows. The adaptive
         gap shrinks, because both lights start closer to 1 and leave less error for their
         different learning rates to act on. The two gaps after eight pear trials are equal at
         about ", gV, " = ", num(gv_cross), "."),
      P("With ", gV, " = .90 the two gaps are nearly equal after eight pear trials, about ",
        num(at(gv90$rw$gap, 8)), " under ", RW, " and ", num(at(gv90$adaptive$gap, 8)), " under
        the adaptive model, but they follow different courses. The ", RW, " gap is largest,
        about ", num(at(gv90$rw$gap, 0)), ", before the first pear trial and shrinks from then
        on, whereas the adaptive gap first grows and then shrinks. A gap produced by
        carried-over learned values is present before the first pear trial. When the lights
        start with equal learned values, a gap produced by unequal associabilities develops only
        during the pear trials."),
      div(class = "question", uiOutput("q3d_claim"), uiOutput("q3d"))),
    conditionalPanel("output.done_q3d",
      h3("How much training, and when to measure"),
      P("In the examples so far, B and D had ten compound trials, and associability changed at
         the rate η = .05. Both settings determine how far B's associability falls before the
         pear trials, and η also applies during the pear trials. Change them and see how the
         gap changes over fifteen pear trials."),
      div(class = "controls-inline",
        sliderInput("n3_compound", "Compound trials", min = 1, max = 20, value = 10, step = 1,
                    ticks = FALSE, width = "260px"),
        sliderInput("n3_eta", HTML("Rate of change of associability, η"), min = .01,
                    max = .05, value = .05, step = .01, ticks = FALSE, width = "260px")),
      uiOutput("n3_text"),
      fig("p3_training", "280px"),
      P("The tutorial varied the number of compound trials from 1 to 20 and η from .01 to
         .05, 100 combinations in all. In every combination, the gap was positive after every
         pear trial, and it was largest between the sixth and the tenth pear trial. The gap stays
         positive more generally, as long as B enters the pear trials with lower associability
         than D, the saliences are equal, the values for the pear start at zero, and the learning
         rates are below 1. D's associability then stays at least as high as B's, so B can narrow
         the gap but cannot overtake D."),
      P("The size and timing of the gap, however, changed with both settings. With ten
         compound trials, lowering η from .05 to .01 reduced the largest gap from about ",
         num(max(base$adaptive$gap)), " to ", num(max(eta_low$adaptive$gap)), " and moved it
         from the ", ordinal(peak_k), " to the ", ordinal(which.max(eta_low$adaptive$gap) - 1),
         " pear trial. We can choose the amount of training in an experiment, but we do not know
         a participant's η in advance, so we do not know on which pear trial the gap will be
         largest. A test only at the end of the pear trials would show whether a difference
         remains, but not when it appeared or how it developed."),
      h3("Which conclusions depend on the rule"),
      P("Under the rule used so far, Equation 3, associability changes in proportion to the
         difference between the two errors and does not change when the errors are equal. This
         matters for
         the comparison light. D and its companion, the new tone C, start with equal values and
         equal saliences, so they make equal errors, and D keeps its associability of .500.
         Equal salience is a modeling assumption, however, and a tone and a light may well
         differ in how noticeable they are. D is a fair comparison light only if it differs from
         B in nothing but its companion's earlier training."),
      P("Mackintosh's proposal can also be written as other rules. Under a rank-based rule,
         associability moves a fixed proportion of the way toward 1 whenever a cue makes the
         smaller error, and toward 0 whenever it makes the larger error. How much smaller or
         larger does not matter. The proportion is set so that B again ends the compound trials
         with associability about ", num(trained$adaptive$alpha_B), "."),
      div(class = "question", uiOutput("q3e"))),
    conditionalPanel("output.done_q3e",
      tags$details(class = "worked-example",
        tags$summary("Compare the rules yourself"),
        div(class = "controls-inline",
          radioButtons("r3_rule", "Rule for associability", choices = setNames(names(rule_names),
                       rule_names)),
          radioButtons("r3_c", "Salience of C", choices = c(
            "Equal to D's" = "0", "One part in a million higher" = "1e-6", "1% higher" = "0.01"))),
        uiOutput("r3_text"),
        fig("p3_rule", "280px")),
      settled("When no learned value for the apple carries over, the difference in
               associability is the only difference between B and D that enters the pear trials,
               so preventing or removing it removes the gap, as it must. Carried-over learned
               value gives Rescorla–Wagner a gap too, but one that is largest before the first
               pear trial. Whether D is a fair comparison light depends on the rule: among the
               three rules, only under Equation 3.",
              "These are all differences in learned values, which we cannot observe. Step 4 asks
               how they would appear in a participant's responses."),
      aside("Section 4, Equations 4 and 5, Figures 4 and 5, Table 5 and Box 3; Supplements S3 and S4.1."))
  )
}


assumptions_server <- function(input, output, answers, add_note) {

  # Prevent, Remove and Supply (Section 4.1).
  pr_choices <- c(gone = "It disappears.", smaller = "It becomes smaller but stays positive.",
                  same = "It stays about the same.")
  supply_choices <- c(same = "The same on every pear trial, because Supply starts with the same learning rates.",
                      close = "Close over the ten pear trials, but different over more pear trials.",
                      smaller = "Much smaller from the first pear trial, because Supply's learning rates cannot change.")
  q3a_items <- list(
    item("pr", "Under Prevent and under Remove, what happens to the B–D gap?", pr_choices),
    item("supply", "How does the gap under Supply compare with the adaptive model's?", supply_choices))
  gap_runs <- function(r) r$adaptive$gap
  unchanged_minus_supply <- gap_runs(runs$none) - gap_runs(runs$supply)
  # How much a light's learned value rises from the tenth to the last pear trial.
  later_rise <- function(r, light) at(r$adaptive[[light]]$V, n_long) - at(r$adaptive[[light]]$V, 10)
  pr_text <- paste0("Under both interventions, B and D start the pear trials with equal learned
    values and equal associabilities, so they learn identically, and the gap stays at zero.
    Under these starting conditions the result is guaranteed, because associability is the only
    difference between B and D that enters the pear trials. Here, Prevent and Remove mainly
    check that the program does what the specification says. They become informative when
    learned values for the apple also carry over.")
  prevent_text <- paste0("Prevent also changes what B learns about the apple. With its
    associability held at .5, B reaches ", num(runs$prevent$trained$adaptive$V_B), ", the same
    value as D, instead of ", num(trained$adaptive$V_B), ". In the adaptive model, B learns less
    about the apple than D only because its associability falls. If the learned values for the
    apple carried over in full, Prevent would still give no gap, whereas Remove would leave B
    behind D by about ", num(at(remove_carried$adaptive$gap, 0)), " before the first pear trial,
    because the two interventions alter the model at different times.")
  supply_text <- paste0("On the first pear trial, a light's own error and the error of
    predicting zero are both 1, so its associability does not change, and the second pear trial
    uses the same learning rate as the first. Supply and the adaptive model therefore give the
    same gaps after one and after two pear trials, about ", num(at(gap_runs(runs$supply), 1)),
    " after the first. From the second pear trial on, the adaptive model's associabilities rise,
    D's faster than B's during the ten pear trials of the task, while Supply's learning rates stay
    fixed. Over these ten pear trials the two gaps never differ by more than about ",
    num(max(abs(unchanged_minus_supply[1:11]))), ". Over more pear trials, B's learning rate
    keeps rising under the adaptive model, while Supply keeps it at ",
    num(trained$adaptive$rate_B), ". B still has much of the pear left to learn, so over the next
    ten pear trials its value rises by ", num(later_rise(runs$none, "B")), " under the adaptive
    model and by ", num(later_rise(runs$supply, "B")), " under Supply. D's value is already
    closer to 1 and rises by about the same amount under both, by ",
    num(later_rise(runs$none, "D")), " and by ", num(later_rise(runs$supply, "D")), ". After
    twenty pear trials the gap is therefore ",
    num(at(gap_runs(runs$supply), n_long)), " under Supply and ", num(at(gap_runs(runs$none), n_long)),
    " under the adaptive model. Because Supply assigns the learning rates directly, it cannot
    show how they arose.")
  ask_server("q3a", input, output, answers, q3a_items, button = "See the four runs",
    feedback = function(a) tagList(
      if (a$pr != "gone") p("Under Prevent and Remove, B and D enter the pear trials in the same
        state, with no difference left for the gap to come from."),
      P(pr_text),
      P(prevent_text),
      if (a$supply == "same") p("The two runs agree only at first.")
      else if (a$supply == "smaller") p("Supply starts with the same learning rates as the
        adaptive model, so its first gaps are the same."),
      P(supply_text)),
    on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 3", "Changing the model",
      "What happens to the gap under Prevent, Remove and Supply?",
      paste0("Prevent and Remove: ", pr_choices[[a$pr]], " Supply: ", supply_choices[[a$supply]]),
      result = paste0("Prevent and Remove give no gap. Supply gives ", num(at(gap_runs(runs$supply), 1)),
        " after one pear trial, as the adaptive model does. Largest difference over ten pear trials: ",
        num(max(abs(unchanged_minus_supply[1:11]))), ". After twenty pear trials: ",
        num(at(gap_runs(runs$supply), n_long)), " against ", num(at(gap_runs(runs$none), n_long)), "."),
      settings = paste0(first_set(), "; Prevent, Remove and Supply over ", n_long, " pear trials")))
  output$p3_runs <- renderPlot({
    req(answers$q3a)
    plot_gap_runs(list(Unchanged = gap_runs(runs$none), Supply = gap_runs(runs$supply),
                       "Prevent, Remove" = gap_runs(runs$prevent)),
                  title = "The B–D gap under the adaptive model and the three interventions",
                  subtitle = "Unchanged: the adaptive model of Step 2. Shaded: pear trials beyond the ten of the task",
                  shade_after = default_settings$n_pear, ylim = c(-.02, .32))
  })

  # The carryover of associability.
  ga_run <- reactive(run_inquiry(settings_with(g_alpha = input$ga)))
  output$ga_text <- renderUI({
    req(input$ga)
    r <- ga_run(); g <- input$ga
    P("With ", gA, " = ", axis_num(g), ", B enters the pear trials with associability ",
      num(r$start$alpha_B), " and D with ", num(r$start$alpha_D), ". The gap is ",
      prob(at(r$adaptive$gap, 1)), " after the first pear trial and ", prob(at(r$adaptive$gap, 8)),
      " after eight.")
  })
  output$p3_ga <- renderPlot({
    req(input$ga)
    plot_gap(ga_run(), ylim = c(-.02, .32), ref = base, ref_label = "Full carryover",
             title = paste0("The B–D gap with associability carryover of ", axis_num(input$ga)))
  })

  # The conclusion so far.
  claim_choices <- c(
    support = "If an experiment finds D ahead of B on the pear trials, that supports the adaptive model over Rescorla–Wagner.",
    depends = "The models disagree under these assumptions. Whether a B–D difference supports the adaptive model depends on what carries over to the pear trials.",
    none = "The two explanations cannot be told apart.")
  q3b_items <- list(item("claim", "Suppose an experiment found that D learned more than B about
    the pear. What would you conclude so far?", claim_choices))
  ask_server("q3b", input, output, answers, q3b_items, button = "Save my conclusion",
    feedback = function(a) p("Your notes now keep this conclusion. See whether you would keep
      it once learned value may carry over."),
    on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 3", "Your conclusion so far", q3b_items[[1]]$label,
      claim_choices[[a$claim]], settings = first_set()))

  # Box 3: Rescorla-Wagner with full value carryover.
  ahead_choices <- c(D = "D.", B = "B.", neither = "Neither: they start equal.")
  gains_choices <- c(B = "B.", D = "D.", equal = "They gain the same.")
  after_choices <- c(D = "D.", B = "B.", equal = "Neither: their values are equal.")
  q3c_items <- list(
    item("ahead", paste0("Under ", RW, ", B ended the compound trials with a learned value for
      the apple of about ", num(trained$rw$V_B), ", and D with about ", num(trained$rw$V_D),
      ". Suppose these values carry over in full (", gV, " = 1). Which light starts the pear
      trials ahead?"), ahead_choices),
    item("gains", "Which light gains more on its first pear trial?", gains_choices),
    item("after", "Which light has the higher learned value after the first pear trial?",
         after_choices))
  q3c_text <- paste0("D starts ahead, at about ", num(at(gv1$rw$D$V, 0)), " against ",
    num(at(gv1$rw$B$V, 0)), ". Both have the learning rate .12, so the light with more of the
    pear left to learn gains more. B gains about .12 × (1 − ", num(at(gv1$rw$B$V, 0)),
    ") ≈ ", num(at(gv1$rw$B$gain, 0)), " on the first pear trial, and D only about .12
    × (1 − ", num(at(gv1$rw$D$V, 0)), ") ≈ ", num(at(gv1$rw$D$gain, 0)), ". D
    nevertheless stays ahead, because it started higher. Each light's remaining error shrinks by
    12% on every pear trial, and so does the difference between their values. The gap is
    therefore largest before the first pear trial.")
  ask_server("q3c", input, output, answers, q3c_items,
    reason = "What makes you think so? (optional)", button = paste0("See what Rescorla–Wagner predicts"),
    feedback = function(a) tagList(
      if (a$ahead != "D") p("Carryover keeps the same fraction of each light's value for the
        apple, so it keeps their order: D, with the higher value, starts ahead."),
      if (a$gains != "B") p("B gains more, because it starts lower."),
      if (a$after != "D") p("D still has the higher value: it gains less, but it started much
        higher."),
      P(q3c_text)),
    on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 3", "Rescorla–Wagner with full value carryover",
      "With g_V = 1, which light starts ahead, which gains more on the first pear trial, and which is ahead after it?",
      paste0("Starts ahead: ", ahead_choices[[a$ahead]], " Gains more: ", gains_choices[[a$gains]],
             " Ahead after the first pear trial: ", after_choices[[a$after]],
             if (nzchar(a$reason)) paste0(" Reason: ", a$reason)),
      result = q3c_text, settings = paste0(first_set(settings_with(g_V = 1)))))

  # The carryover of learned value.
  gv_run <- reactive(run_inquiry(settings_with(g_V = input$gv)))
  output$gv_text <- renderUI({
    req(answers$q3c, input$gv)
    r <- gv_run(); g <- input$gv
    P("With ", gV, " = ", axis_num(g), ", ",
      if (g == 0) "B and D both start the pear trials at zero, so neither model has a gap before
        the first pear trial. "
      else paste0("the gap before the first pear trial is already ", num(at(r$rw$gap, 0)),
        " under ", RW, " (B starts at ", num(at(r$rw$B$V, 0)), ", D at ", num(at(r$rw$D$V, 0)),
        ") and ", num(at(r$adaptive$gap, 0)), " under the adaptive model. "),
      "After eight pear trials the gaps are ", prob(at(r$rw$gap, 8)), " (", RW, ") and ",
      num(at(r$adaptive$gap, 8)), " (adaptive model). Above about ", gV, " = ", num(gv_cross),
      ", ", RW, " gives the larger gap after eight pear trials.")
  })
  output$p3_gap <- renderPlot({
    req(answers$q3c, input$gv)
    plot_gap(gv_run(), ylim = c(-.02, .35),
             title = paste0("The B–D gap with value carryover of ", axis_num(input$gv)))
  })
  output$p3_grid <- renderPlot({
    req(answers$q3c, input$gv)
    plot_gap_by_gV(gv_grid, input$gv, cross = gv_cross)
  })

  # Keeping or changing the earlier conclusion.
  output$q3d_claim <- renderUI({
    req(answers$q3b)
    if (!is.null(answers$q3d)) return(NULL)
    tagList(p(class = "item-label", "Earlier you chose this conclusion:"),
            tags$blockquote(HTML(claim_choices[[answers$q3b$claim]])))
  })
  change_choices <- c(
    keep = "Keep it as it is.",
    qualify = "Under the first assumptions the models predict different B–D gaps. Once learned values for the apple may carry over, both models can predict a positive gap, but they may still differ in when the gap first appears.",
    useless = "The comparison is useless, because both explanations can produce a positive gap, so no B–D result can tell them apart.")
  q3d_items <- list(item("rev", "Would you keep your earlier conclusion or change it?",
                         change_choices))
  ask_server("q3d", input, output, answers, q3d_items,
    reason = "You can also put the conclusion in your own words",
    button = "Save my conclusion",
    feedback = function(a) {
      earlier <- answers$q3b$claim
      tagList(
        p(class = "answered-label", "Your earlier conclusion"),
        tags$blockquote(HTML(claim_choices[[earlier]])),
        if (earlier == "support" && a$rev != "keep") P("With carried-over learned value, ", RW,
          " also puts D ahead of B, so a B–D difference alone no longer favors the adaptive
          model."),
        P(switch(a$rev,
          keep = switch(earlier,
            support = paste0("With carried-over learned value, ", RW, " also puts D ahead of B,
              and above about ", gV, " = ", num(gv_cross), " its gap after eight pear trials is
              the larger one. A B–D difference alone no longer favors the adaptive model."),
            depends = paste0("Your earlier conclusion already allowed for this. The calculations
              show one way it matters: carried-over learned value gives ", RW, " a gap too."),
            none = "Under the first assumptions the explanations disagree. With carried-over
              value both can give a gap, so the size of a difference alone does not tell them
              apart. A gap from carried-over values is there before the first pear trial. A gap
              from associability, with equal starting values, appears only during the pear
              trials. We can still ask when the gap first appears."),
          qualify = "Recording the first response lets you check whether a difference is already
            present before any pear trial. Whether the responses would show it depends on how
            learned values become responses, which Step 4 examines.",
          useless = paste0("You can still use the timing of the gap. With carried-over value, the ",
            RW, " gap is largest before the first pear trial and then shrinks. With no
            carried-over value, the adaptive gap starts at zero and grows over the first pear
            trials. To examine that difference, you need responses from the first pear trial and
            a response measure that can express it."))))
    },
    on_submit = function(a) {
      g <- input$gv; r <- gv_run()
      add_note("Step 3", "Keeping or changing your conclusion", "Would you keep or change your conclusion?",
        paste0("Before: ", claim_choices[[answers$q3b$claim]], " After: ", change_choices[[a$rev]],
               if (nzchar(a$reason)) paste0(" Your own version: ", a$reason)),
        result = paste0("With g_V = 0: ", RW, " gap ", prob(at(base$rw$gap, 8)),
          " and adaptive gap ", num(at(base$adaptive$gap, 8)), " after eight pear trials. With g_V = ",
          axis_num(g), ", the value you were looking at: ", RW, " gap ", prob(at(r$rw$gap, 0)),
          " before the first pear trial and ", prob(at(r$rw$gap, 8)),
          " after eight, adaptive gap ", num(at(r$adaptive$gap, 8)), " after eight."),
        settings = paste0(first_set(settings_with(g_V = g)), "; compared with g_V = 0"),
        open = "Real learners may carry over learned value, associability, both, or neither.")
    })

  # The amount of training and the rate eta (Section 4.3).
  training_run <- reactive({
    req(input$n3_compound, input$n3_eta)
    run_inquiry(settings_with(n_compound = input$n3_compound, eta = input$n3_eta), n = 15)
  })
  output$n3_text <- renderUI({
    r <- training_run(); g <- r$adaptive$gap
    P("With ", input$n3_compound, " compound ", if (input$n3_compound == 1) "trial" else "trials",
      " and η = ", axis_num(input$n3_eta), ", B enters the pear trials with associability ",
      num(r$start$alpha_B), " and D with ", num(r$start$alpha_D), ". The gap is largest after ",
      pear_trials(which.max(g) - 1), ", at about ", num(max(g)), ".")
  })
  output$p3_training <- renderPlot({
    r <- training_run()
    plot_gap_runs(list("Your setting" = r$adaptive$gap, "10 compound trials, η = .05" = base15$adaptive$gap),
                  title = "The adaptive model's gap over fifteen pear trials",
                  ylim = c(-.02, .32), mark_peak = TRUE)
  })

  # The rule for associability (Section 4.4).
  same_choices <- c(same = "About the same.", smaller = "Much smaller.", larger = "Much larger.")
  q3e_items <- list(
    item("prop", "Under the rule used so far, Equation 3, if C is one part in a million more
      salient than D, what happens to the largest B–D gap?", same_choices),
    item("rank", "And under the rank-based rule?", same_choices))
  rule_row <- function(rule) {
    r <- rule_runs[[rule]]
    largest <- function(g) if (max(g) < 1e-12) "no gap" else
      paste0(num(max(g)), " (", which.max(g) - 1, ")")
    vrow(rule_names[[rule]], num(r$matched$alpha_D), num(r$mismatched$alpha_D),
         largest(r$matched$gap), largest(r$mismatched$gap))
  }
  rules_table <- function() tagList(
    p(class = "table-note", "D's associability after the compound trials, and the largest B–D
      gap during fifteen pear trials. The number in parentheses is the pear trial after which
      the gap is largest."),
    div(class = "scroll-x", tabindex = "0", role = "region", `aria-label` = "Three rules",
      tags$table(class = "values",
        tags$thead(
          tags$tr(tags$th("Rule for associability"), tags$th("D's associability, matched"),
                  tags$th("D's associability, C more salient"), tags$th("Largest gap, matched"),
                  tags$th("Largest gap, C more salient"))),
        tags$tbody(rule_row("proportional"), rule_row("rank"), rule_row("rank_ties")))),
    p(class = "table-note", "Matched: C and D have equal saliences. C more salient: by one part in
      a million. Under every rule, B ends the compound trials with associability about .235."))
  rank_r <- rule_runs$rank
  rule_text <- paste0("Under Equation 3, a tiny salience difference makes D's error differ from
    C's by a tiny amount, so D's associability changes by a similarly tiny amount. Even if C is 1%
    more salient than D, D's associability ends the compound trials at about ",
    num(one_percent$alpha_D), " instead of .500, and the gap after eight pear trials changes by
    about ", num(abs(at(one_percent$gap, 8) - at(base$adaptive$gap, 8))), ".")
  rank_text <- paste0("Under the rank-based rule, with C and D matched exactly, the gap is largest
    after ", pear_trials(which.max(rank_r$matched$gap) - 1), ", at about ",
    num(max(rank_r$matched$gap)), ". This differs from Equation 3 although the lights start the
    pear trials with the same associabilities. Under the rank-based rule, a light's associability
    rises by the same fraction of its remaining distance to 1 on every pear trial after the first,
    so the difference between D's and B's associabilities shrinks. Under Equation 3, a light's
    associability rises by η times its learned value, so during the ten pear trials the
    difference grows. If C is more salient than D, whether by one part in a million or by 1%, D
    makes the larger error on every compound trial after the first, so its associability falls
    on each of them, to about ", num(rank_r$mismatched$alpha_D), ". The
    largest gap is then only about ", num(max(rank_r$mismatched$gap)), ". If the rule also lowered
    associability when the errors are equal, as Mackintosh proposed, D would lose as much
    associability during the CD+ trials as B does during the AB+ trials, and there would be no gap
    at all. Among these rules, D is a fair comparison light only under Equation 3.")
  ask_server("q3e", input, output, answers, q3e_items, button = "See the three rules",
    feedback = function(a) tagList(
      if (a$prop != "same") p("Under Equation 3, the size of the change in
        associability follows the size of the difference between the errors."),
      if (a$rank != "smaller") p("Under the rank-based rule, any difference between the errors,
        however small, changes associability by the full step, so D's associability falls on
        almost every compound trial and the gap shrinks."),
      rules_table(),
      P(rule_text),
      P(rank_text)),
    on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 3", "The rule for associability",
      "If C is one part in a million more salient than D, what happens to the largest gap under each rule?",
      paste0("Equation 3: ", same_choices[[a$prop]], " Rank-based rule: ",
             same_choices[[a$rank]]),
      result = paste(rule_text, rank_text), settings = paste0(first_set(), "; fifteen pear trials; rank-based step ",
                                            num(rank_step(), 4))))

  # Comparing the rules freely, after the question.
  rule_run <- reactive({
    req(input$r3_rule, input$r3_c)
    rule_comparison(input$r3_rule, as.numeric(input$r3_c))
  })
  output$r3_text <- renderUI({
    req(answers$q3e)
    r <- rule_run(); g <- r$gap
    P("D's associability after the compound trials is ", num(r$alpha_D), ", and B's ",
      num(r$alpha_B), ". ", if (max(g) < 1e-12) "There is no gap." else paste0("The gap is
      largest after ", pear_trials(which.max(g) - 1), ", at about ", num(max(g)), "."))
  })
  output$p3_rule <- renderPlot({
    req(answers$q3e)
    r <- rule_run()
    plot_gap_runs(list("Chosen rule" = r$gap,
                       "Equation 3, matched" = rule_runs$proportional$matched$gap),
                  title = "The B–D gap over fifteen pear trials", ylim = c(-.02, .32))
  })

  # Starting the inquiry again clears the answers but keeps the notes.
  list(reset = function() clear_answers(answers, c("q3a", "q3b", "q3c", "q3d", "q3e")))
}

content:
# Step 4: from model states to behavior (Section 5)
# What would be recorded, the question of Box 4, the sigmoid and threshold
# response functions, where the difference in behavior is largest (with Table
# 6 shown in full once that question is answered), and whether more responses
# would show the difference.

behavior_ui <- function() {
  scene("scene-4", "4", "From model states to behavior", "output.done_q3e", "done_q4c",
    "A response function can enlarge, reduce or hide a difference in learned values. With the lights starting at zero, the first responses are equally likely to be yes under any shared response function.",
    p("Learned values, associabilities and the B–D gap are quantities inside a model, and we
       cannot observe any of them directly. In the task, we would instead show a light, ask
       whether the pear will follow, and record a yes or a no before it appears."),
    h3("What we would observe"),
    P("We continue with the pear trials of Step 2, in which ", B_gloss, " and ", D_gloss, " are
       each presented alone on ten trials. On each trial, before the pear appears, the
       participant answers whether they expect the pear, and we record the response, yes or no.
       In the models, learned values change when the pear appears, not when the question is
       asked, although in a real experiment being asked might itself change what participants
       learn."),
    p("To predict these responses, we need a response function that turns a learned value into
       the probability of a yes response. Each response is numbered by the pear trial on which
       it is given. The response on pear trial 7, for example, comes before the seventh pear
       appears, so it depends on the learned value after six completed pear trials. The response
       function belongs to the observation bridge, which links model states to responses and
       also covers what is recorded and when. The learning rules specify how learned values
       change, but not how they relate to a yes response."),
    p("For now, we assume that the same function applies to both lights, and that the
       probability of a yes response depends only on the light's learned value. The learning
       models do not imply either assumption. A participant might be more inclined to answer yes
       to one light than to the other at the same learned value. Step 6 returns to this
       possibility."),
    div(class = "question", uiOutput("q4a")),
    conditionalPanel("output.done_q4a",
      h3("Two response functions, different predicted behavior"),
      p("A response function may be part of a psychological theory of responding, as in the
         choice rule of Luce (1959), or an additional assumption linking learned values to a
         particular measure. In either case, its form and parameters need support from a theory
         of responding, from independent data, or from both. For example, in these models a cue
         that has never been followed by an outcome has learned value zero. Yes responses to
         such a cue could help estimate the probability of a yes at learned value zero, provided
         the same function applies to it. We consider two forms:"),
      tags$ul(
        tags$li("The sigmoid: the probability of a yes rises gradually with the learned value.
                 It is .5 at the learned value θ = .5, and γ = 8 sets how steeply it rises around
                 that value."),
        tags$li("The threshold rule: the participant answers yes whenever the learned value
                 exceeds θ = .5, and no otherwise.")),
      response_formulas_ui(),
      fig("p4_functions", "320px"),
      div(class = "scroll-x", tabindex = "0", role = "region",
          `aria-label` = "Learned values and predicted behavior", uiOutput("resp_table")),
      h3("Which behavior to measure, and when"),
      div(class = "question", uiOutput("q4b"))),
    conditionalPanel("output.done_q4b",
      P("On pear trial 1, both lights have learned value zero for the pear. Under any response
         function shared by the two lights, they therefore have the same probability of a yes on
         their first pear trial, even though their associabilities differ. Under the sigmoid this
         probability is about ", num(responses$p_B[1]), ", not zero. Associability affects only
         how much a light learns from the pear, and the first response comes before the pear has
         appeared with that light. If learned values for the apple carried over, as in Step 3,
         the lights could already differ on their first pear trial."),
      fig("p4_differences", "300px"),
      P("We calculate the difference in yes probabilities by applying the response function to
         each light's learned value and then subtracting, not by applying the function to the
         B–D gap. Under the adaptive model, the gap in learned value is largest after ",
         pear_trials(peak_k), ", just before the response on pear trial ", peak_k + 1, ", whereas
         under the sigmoid the difference in yes probabilities is largest at the response on pear
         trial ", peak_yes + 1, ", after ", pear_trials(peak_yes), ". The figure numbers the
         responses by pear trial, so the two peaks appear at ", peak_k + 1, " and ", peak_yes + 1,
         "."),
      P("The sigmoid is flatter near its lower and upper ends, so the same difference in learned
         value produces a smaller difference in probability there. After six pear trials, B's
         value (", num(responses$V_B[7]), ") and D's (", num(responses$V_D[7]), ") lie on either
         side of the steep middle of the sigmoid. After eight, D's value (",
         num(responses$V_D[9]), ") has moved onto the flatter upper part. The pear trial on
         which this difference peaks therefore depends on θ and γ. Under the
         threshold rule, the two lights' predicted responses differ only on pear trials ",
         min(threshold_window) + 1, " to ", max(threshold_window) + 1, ", the shaded band in the
         figure."),
      P("Equal B–D gaps need not give equal differences in behavior. With ", gV, " = .90
         (Step 3), the two models had nearly equal gaps after eight pear trials, about ",
         num(at(gv90$rw$gap, 8)), " under ", RW, " and ", num(at(gv90$adaptive$gap, 8)), " under
         the adaptive model. The learned values themselves differ, however. They are about ",
         num(at(gv90$rw$B$V, 8)), " for B and ", num(at(gv90$rw$D$V, 8)), " for D under ", RW,
         ", and ", num(at(gv90$adaptive$B$V, 8)), " and ", num(at(gv90$adaptive$D$V, 8)), " under
         the adaptive model. With the sigmoid, the yes probabilities then differ by about ",
         num(yes_gap(gv90$rw, 8)), " under ", RW, " but by only about ",
         num(yes_gap(gv90$adaptive, 8)), " under the adaptive model, whose values lie on the
         flatter upper part of the curve."),
      div(class = "question", uiOutput("q4c"))),
    conditionalPanel("output.done_q4c",
      tags$details(class = "worked-example",
        tags$summary("Try another response function or response"),
        p(class = "muted", "Each try is added to the table below and to your notes."),
        div(class = "controls-inline",
          radioButtons("q4_try_rule", "Response function", inline = TRUE,
                       choices = c("Sigmoid" = "sigmoid", "Threshold" = "threshold")),
          sliderInput("q4_try_q", "Response on pear trial", min = 1, max = 10, value = 1, step = 1,
                      ticks = FALSE, width = "260px")),
        actionButton("q4_try_go", "Show", class = "btn-submit"),
        uiOutput("q4_tries")),
      settled("A response function can enlarge, reduce or hide a difference in learned values,
               and where the difference in behavior is largest depends on it. With the lights
               starting the pear trials at zero, their first responses are equally likely to be
               yes under any shared response function.",
              "What an experiment could establish from responses, each a random yes or no.
               Step 5 simulates such an experiment."),
      aside("Section 5, Equations 6 and 7, Table 6, Figure 6 and Box 4."))
  )
}

# The difference in sigmoid yes probabilities, D minus B, after k pear trials.
yes_gap <- function(m, k) response_prob(at(m$D$V, k), "sigmoid") - response_prob(at(m$B$V, k), "sigmoid")


behavior_server <- function(input, output, answers, add_note) {

  # Box 4: after five pear trials.
  five <- responses[responses$k == 5, ]
  likely_choices <- c(
    depends = "It depends on how learned values are turned into responses. Under a function that rises with learned value, a yes to D is at least as likely as a yes to B.",
    value = paste0("B gets a yes with probability ", num(five$V_B), ", and D with probability ",
                   num(five$V_D), "."),
    same = "They are equally likely, because both lights started the pear trials at zero.")
  must_choices <- c(
    yes = "Yes, because B's learned value is below .5 and D's above it.",
    only = "Only if the response function is deterministic, for example a yes for every learned value above .5 and a no below it.",
    never = "No. A response is never certain, whatever the rule.")
  q4a_items <- list(
    item("likely", paste0("After five pear trials, the adaptive model gives B a learned value of
      about ", num(five$V_B), " and D about ", num(five$V_D), ". How likely is a participant to
      answer yes to each light on the next pear trial?"), likely_choices),
    item("must", "Must the participant answer no to B and yes to D?", must_choices))
  q4a_text <- paste0("Under the sigmoid described below, with slope γ = 8 and midpoint
    θ = .5, B's value of ", num(five$V_B), " gives a yes probability of 1/{1 +
    exp[−8(", num(five$V_B), " − .5)]} ≈ ", num(five$p_B), ", and D's value of ",
    num(five$V_D), " gives about ", num(five$p_D), ". The learned values differ by about ",
    num(five$V_D - five$V_B), ", whereas the probabilities differ by about ",
    num(five$p_D - five$p_B), ". A participant may still answer yes to B, although the
    probability is only ", num(five$p_B), ", or answer no to D. Under a threshold rule at .5, the
    participant answers no to B and yes to D.")
  ask_server("q4a", input, output, answers, q4a_items,
    reason = "What else would you need to assume to answer these questions? (optional)",
    button = "See two response functions",
    feedback = function(a) tagList(
      if (a$likely == "value") p("A learned value is not a probability of a yes, just as the
        light's value of .1303 in Step 1 did not imply a 13% probability of a yes.")
      else if (a$likely == "same") p("The lights started equal, but after five pear trials their
        learned values differ."),
      if (a$must == "yes") p("Only a deterministic rule, such as a threshold at .5, makes these
        responses certain. Under a response function that rises gradually, either response can
        occur.")
      else if (a$must == "never") p("A threshold rule does make them certain. Whether a response
        is certain depends on the response function."),
      P(q4a_text),
      p("To answer either question, we have to assume a response function.")),
    on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 4", "Would a difference in learning be visible?",
      q4a_items[[1]]$label,
      paste0(likely_choices[[a$likely]], " Must: ", must_choices[[a$must]],
             if (nzchar(a$reason)) paste0(" Further assumption: ", a$reason)),
      result = q4a_text, settings = paste0(first_set(), "; sigmoid with gamma = 8, theta = .5")))

  # Table 6. Until the question about the largest difference is answered, it
  # shows the learned values only.
  output$resp_table <- renderUI({
    req(answers$q4a)
    full <- !is.null(answers$q4b)
    yn <- function(x) ifelse(x == 1, "yes", "no")
    pair <- function(b, d) paste0(b, " / ", d)
    tagList(
      p(class = "table-note", if (full) "The adaptive model: learned values and predicted
        behavior before each response. Each cell gives B first and D second." else "The
        adaptive model: learned values before each response. Each cell gives B first and D
        second."),
      tags$table(class = "values",
        tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th("Response on pear trial"), tags$th("Completed pear trials"),
                           tags$th("Learned value"),
                           if (full) tagList(tags$th("Yes probability, sigmoid"),
                                             tags$th("Predicted response, threshold")))),
        tags$tbody(lapply(seq_len(nrow(responses)), function(i) {
          r <- responses[i, ]
          do.call(vrow, c(list(r$k + 1, r$k, pair(num(r$V_B), num(r$V_D))),
            if (full) list(pair(num(r$p_B), num(r$p_D)), pair(yn(r$t_B), yn(r$t_D)))))
        }))),
      p(class = "table-note", "Probabilities are calculated from unrounded learned values. The
        response on each pear trial is recorded before the pear appears on that trial."))
  })
  output$p4_functions <- renderPlot({
    req(answers$q4a)
    plot_response_functions(responses, points = !is.null(answers$q4b))
  })

  # Where the difference in behavior is largest.
  rule_choices <- c(sigmoid = "Sigmoid", threshold = "Threshold")
  peak_choices <- c(`1` = "On pear trial 1.", `6` = "On pear trial 6.", `10` = "On pear trial 10.",
                    same = "The same on all three.")
  q4b_items <- list(
    item("rule", "Choose a response function.", rule_choices),
    item("peak", "Of the responses on pear trials 1, 6 and 10, where is the difference between
      D's and B's yes probabilities largest?", peak_choices))
  # The differences on pear trials 1, 6 and 10, and where the largest is
  # ("same" when all three are equal).
  largest_at <- function(rule) {
    q <- c(1, 6, 10)
    p <- function(V) response_prob(V, rule)
    d <- p(responses$V_D[q]) - p(responses$V_B[q])
    top <- as.character(q[abs(d - max(d)) < 1e-12])
    list(d = d, top = if (length(top) == length(q)) "same" else top)
  }
  q4b_feedback <- function(a) {
    pattern <- largest_at(a$rule)
    tagList(
      if (!(a$peak %in% pattern$top)) p(switch(a$peak,
        `1` = "Associability affects learning from the pear. It does not give either light a
          value for the pear before the first pear trial. Both start at zero, so the first yes
          probabilities are equal.",
        `10` = if (a$rule == "sigmoid") "By pear trial 10, D's yes probability is near the top
          of the sigmoid, while B's is rising through the steep middle, so the probabilities
          come closer." else "By pear trial 10, both values are above .5, so the threshold rule
          gives a yes to both lights.",
        same = "The values and their position on the response function change during the pear
          trials, so the difference changes too.",
        `6` = "")),
      P("Under the ", if (a$rule == "sigmoid") "sigmoid" else "threshold rule",
        ", the difference is ", prob(pattern$d[1]), " on pear trial 1, ", prob(pattern$d[2]),
        " on pear trial 6 and ", prob(pattern$d[3]), " on pear trial 10.",
        if (a$rule == "sigmoid") paste0(" Across all ten responses it is largest on pear trial ",
          peak_yes + 1, ".") else paste0(" Across all ten responses, the threshold rule gives
          different responses only on pear trials ", min(threshold_window) + 1, " to ",
          max(threshold_window) + 1, "."),
        " The table and the plot of the response functions now show both lights' yes
        probabilities."))
  }
  ask_server("q4b", input, output, answers, q4b_items, button = "See the differences",
    feedback = q4b_feedback,
    on_submit = function(a) {
      pattern <- largest_at(a$rule)
      add_note("Step 4", "Where the difference in behavior is largest",
        paste0("With the ", if (a$rule == "sigmoid") "sigmoid" else "threshold rule", ": ",
               q4b_items[[2]]$label),
        peak_choices[[a$peak]],
        result = paste0("Difference in yes probability, D minus B: ", prob(pattern$d[1]),
          " on pear trial 1, ", prob(pattern$d[2]), " on pear trial 6 and ", prob(pattern$d[3]),
          " on pear trial 10."),
        settings = paste0(first_set(), "; ", rule_set(a$rule)))
    })
  output$p4_differences <- renderPlot({ req(answers$q4b); plot_response_differences(responses) })

  # Would more responses show the difference?
  more_choices <- c(yes = "Yes.", no = "No.")
  q4c_items <- list(
    item("sig", "Under the sigmoid, could responses from more participants on pear trial 10 show
      the difference between B and D?", more_choices),
    item("thr", "Under the threshold rule?", more_choices))
  ten <- responses[responses$k == 9, ]
  q4c_text <- paste0("Under the sigmoid, which always rises as the learned value increases,
    different learned values give different yes probabilities: ", num(ten$p_B), " for B and ",
    num(ten$p_D), " for D on pear trial 10. Each response is a random draw, so in a small
    sample D need not get more yes responses than B, but with more responses from comparable
    participants we could estimate even a small difference more precisely. Under the threshold
    rule, both lights have a yes probability of 1 on pear trial 10, so more responses from
    participants who learn like this would show no difference at that point, although earlier
    responses could. A different measure, such as a rating of how strongly the participant
    expects the pear, could also show the difference, if its relationship to learned value were
    specified and justified.")
  ask_server("q4c", input, output, answers, q4c_items,
    feedback = function(a) tagList(
      if (a$sig == "no") p("Under the sigmoid the two probabilities differ, so more responses
        estimate that difference more precisely."),
      if (a$thr == "yes") p("With these learned values, the threshold rule gives a yes to both
        lights on pear trial 10, so more participants who learn like this add only more yes
        responses."),
      P(q4c_text)),
    on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 4", "Would more responses show the difference?",
      "On pear trial 10, could more responses show the difference between B and D?",
      paste0("Sigmoid: ", more_choices[[a$sig]], " Threshold rule: ", more_choices[[a$thr]]),
      result = q4c_text, settings = first_set(),
      open = "What could an experiment with random yes-or-no responses establish?"))

  # Further tries of a function and a response.
  q4_tries <- reactiveVal(list())
  try_values <- function(rule, q) {
    V_B <- responses$V_B[q]; V_D <- responses$V_D[q]
    list(rule = rule, q = q, V_B = V_B, V_D = V_D,
         p_B = response_prob(V_B, rule), p_D = response_prob(V_D, rule))
  }
  observeEvent(input$q4_try_go, {
    req(answers$q4c, input$q4_try_rule, input$q4_try_q)
    v <- try_values(input$q4_try_rule, input$q4_try_q)
    q4_tries(c(q4_tries(), list(v)))
    add_note("Step 4", "Another function or response",
      paste0(rule_choices[[v$rule]], ", response on pear trial ", v$q, "."), "Viewed.",
      result = paste0("Probability of a yes ", prob(v$p_B), " for B and ", prob(v$p_D),
                      " for D, a difference of ", prob(v$p_D - v$p_B), "."),
      settings = paste0(first_set(), "; ", rule_set(v$rule), "; response on pear trial ", v$q))
  })
  output$q4_tries <- renderUI({
    tries <- q4_tries()
    if (!length(tries)) return(NULL)
    tagList(
      p(class = "table-note", "Probability of a yes at the response"),
      div(class = "scroll-x", tabindex = "0", role = "region",
          `aria-label` = "Probabilities of a yes for each try", tags$table(class = "values",
        tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th("Function"), tags$th("Pear trial"),
                           tags$th(class = "cue-B", "B"), tags$th(class = "cue-D", "D"),
                           tags$th("D minus B"))),
        tags$tbody(lapply(tries, function(v) tags$tr(
          tags$td(rule_choices[[v$rule]]), tags$td(v$q), tags$td(prob(v$p_B)),
          tags$td(prob(v$p_D)), tags$td(prob(v$p_D - v$p_B))))))),
      p(class = "table-note", "Differences are calculated from unrounded values."))
  })

  # Starting the inquiry again clears the answers and the tries but keeps the
  # notes.
  list(reset = function() {
    clear_answers(answers, c("q4a", "q4b", "q4c"))
    q4_tries(list())
  })
}

# Model engine for the companion app
#
# These functions compute every model result the app shows, except the
# simulated experiments of Steps 5 and 6, which are read from
# data/inference_cases.rds. They call the learning models in models.R (a copy
# of R/models.R) and add only what the app needs: the two training histories,
# the pear trials, the carryover assumptions, the changes to the adaptive
# model, the rank-based rule, the response functions, and the decision model
# of Step 7.
#
# The cues are named as in the paper: tones A and C, lights B and D, and the
# buzzer X. A is trained first and then appears with B; X is trained first,
# and the new tone C appears with D, the comparison light.
#
# Checked against the paper's values by tests/verify_app.R.

# From the repository root this is R/models.R; from shiny_app/ it is the copy in
# shiny_app/R/models.R, which the tests require to be identical.
source("R/models.R", local = TRUE)

# The settings of the paper's examples.
default_settings <- list(
  beta = .12,                           # Rescorla-Wagner learning rate (Section 2.2)
  S = .3, alpha_init = .5, eta = .05,   # adaptive model (Section 3.2)
  n_first = 10, n_compound = 10, n_pear = 10,
  g_V = 0, g_alpha = 1,                 # carryover to the pear trials (Section 4.2)
  change = "none",                      # none, prevent, remove or supply (Section 4.1)
  c_offset = 0                          # tone C's salience is S * (1 + c_offset) (Section 4.4)
)

settings_with <- function(...) modifyList(default_settings, list(...))

# The two training histories of Table 1, all trials followed by the apple:
# ten A+ then ten AB+, and ten X+ then ten CD+.
trained_tone_history <- function(s) c(make_trials("A", 1, s$n_first, "Earlier trials"),
                                      make_trials(c("A", "B"), 1, s$n_compound, "Compound trials"))
new_tone_history <- function(s) c(make_trials("X", 1, s$n_first, "Earlier trials"),
                                  make_trials(c("C", "D"), 1, s$n_compound, "Compound trials"))
rw_rates <- function(cues, s) setNames(rep(s$beta, length(cues)), cues)


# Section 2: the trained-tone history under Rescorla-Wagner

# One row per trial t = 1, ..., 20: the cues present, the values before the
# trial, their combined prediction, the shared error, each cue's gain and the
# values after the trial. The light is absent on the first ten trials, so its
# gain there is NA.
rw_trials <- function(s = default_settings) {
  design <- trained_tone_history(s)
  run <- rw_simulate(design, beta = rw_rates(c("A", "B"), s))
  n <- length(design)
  A <- run$V[run$cue == "A"]   # A[t] is the value before trial t; A[n + 1] the final value
  B <- run$V[run$cue == "B"]
  light <- vapply(design, function(x) "B" %in% x$cues, logical(1))
  prediction <- A[1:n] + ifelse(light, B[1:n], 0)
  data.frame(trial = seq_len(n), light = light,
             V_A = A[1:n], V_B = B[1:n], prediction = prediction, error = 1 - prediction,
             gain_A = A[-1] - A[1:n], gain_B = ifelse(light, B[-1] - B[1:n], NA),
             V_A_after = A[-1], V_B_after = B[-1])
}

# Section 2.3: one compound trial followed by the apple, starting from the
# values V, as specified and as two mistaken programs would calculate it. The
# specified rule is applied by rw_final(). One mistaken program uses each
# cue's own error; the other updates A first and then recalculates the error
# for B. Returns the gains of A and B.
compound_check <- function(V = c(A = .3, B = .3), s = default_settings) {
  rate <- s$beta
  specified <- rw_final(make_trials(c("A", "B"), 1, 1, "Check"), beta = rw_rates(c("A", "B"), s),
                        V_init = V)
  own <- V + rate * (1 - V)
  one_at_a_time <- V
  one_at_a_time["A"] <- V[["A"]] + rate * (1 - sum(V))
  one_at_a_time["B"] <- V[["B"]] + rate * (1 - (one_at_a_time[["A"]] + V[["B"]]))
  list(specified = specified[c("A", "B")] - V, own = own - V, one_at_a_time = one_at_a_time - V)
}


# Sections 3 and 4: what the compound trials leave behind

trained_states <- function(s = default_settings) {
  rw_b <- rw_final(trained_tone_history(s), beta = rw_rates(c("A", "B"), s))
  rw_c <- rw_final(new_tone_history(s), beta = rw_rates(c("X", "C", "D"), s))

  # The adaptive model runs one phase at a time, so that Prevent can hold
  # associability fixed during the compound trials only (Section 4.1). X's
  # trials cannot affect C or D, so the new-tone history starts at its
  # compound trials. B, C and D start at value zero and associability
  # alpha_init. A nonzero c_offset makes C slightly more or less salient than
  # D (Section 4.4).
  eta_compound <- if (s$change == "prevent") 0 else s$eta
  first <- adaptive_final_state(make_trials("A", 1, s$n_first, "Earlier trials"),
                                S = c(A = s$S), alpha_init = c(A = s$alpha_init), eta = s$eta)
  ad_b <- adaptive_final_state(make_trials(c("A", "B"), 1, s$n_compound, "Compound trials"),
                               S = c(A = s$S, B = s$S),
                               alpha_init = c(A = unname(first$alpha), B = s$alpha_init),
                               eta = eta_compound, V_init = c(A = unname(first$V), B = 0))
  ad_c <- adaptive_final_state(make_trials(c("C", "D"), 1, s$n_compound, "Compound trials"),
                               S = c(C = s$S * (1 + s$c_offset), D = s$S),
                               alpha_init = c(C = s$alpha_init, D = s$alpha_init),
                               eta = eta_compound, V_init = c(C = 0, D = 0))

  # The learning rates of Table 3: fixed under Rescorla-Wagner, S * alpha
  # under the adaptive model.
  list(
    rw = list(V_A = unname(rw_b["A"]), V_B = unname(rw_b["B"]), V_D = unname(rw_c["D"]),
              rate_B = s$beta, rate_D = s$beta),
    adaptive = list(V_A_first = unname(first$V), alpha_A_first = unname(first$alpha),
                    V_A = unname(ad_b$V["A"]), V_B = unname(ad_b$V["B"]),
                    V_D = unname(ad_c$V["D"]),
                    alpha_B = unname(ad_b$alpha["B"]), alpha_D = unname(ad_c$alpha["D"]),
                    rate_B = s$S * unname(ad_b$alpha["B"]), rate_D = s$S * unname(ad_c$alpha["D"]))
  )
}

# The compound trials one at a time, for B and for D under both models: the
# value before the trial, the error the light learns from, its learning rate,
# its gain and, under the adaptive model, its associability before and after
# the trial. Row j describes compound trial j. Uses the default history,
# without changes or a salience difference.
compound_trials <- function(s = default_settings) {
  n1 <- s$n_first
  rw_b <- rw_simulate(trained_tone_history(s), beta = rw_rates(c("A", "B"), s))
  rw_c <- rw_simulate(new_tone_history(s), beta = rw_rates(c("X", "C", "D"), s))
  ad_b <- adaptive_simulate(trained_tone_history(s), S = c(A = s$S, B = s$S),
                            alpha_init = c(A = s$alpha_init, B = s$alpha_init), eta = s$eta)
  ad_c <- adaptive_simulate(new_tone_history(s), S = c(X = s$S, C = s$S, D = s$S),
                            alpha_init = c(X = s$alpha_init, C = s$alpha_init, D = s$alpha_init),
                            eta = s$eta)
  # A run holds each cue's state at the start of every trial, so the row of
  # trial t + 1 gives the state after trial t.
  trials <- n1 + seq_len(s$n_compound)
  state <- function(run, cue, col, t) run[[col]][run$cue == cue][t]
  light <- function(rw, ad, cue, companion) {
    V_rw <- state(rw, cue, "V", trials)
    V_ad <- state(ad, cue, "V", trials)
    data.frame(trial = seq_len(s$n_compound),
      rw_V = V_rw, rw_error = 1 - V_rw - state(rw, companion, "V", trials),
      rw_rate = s$beta, rw_gain = state(rw, cue, "V", trials + 1) - V_rw,
      ad_V = V_ad, ad_error = 1 - V_ad,
      ad_companion_error = 1 - state(ad, companion, "V", trials),
      ad_alpha = state(ad, cue, "alpha", trials),
      ad_rate = s$S * state(ad, cue, "alpha", trials),
      ad_gain = state(ad, cue, "V", trials + 1) - V_ad,
      ad_alpha_after = state(ad, cue, "alpha", trials + 1))
  }
  list(B = light(rw_b, ad_b, "B", "A"), D = light(rw_c, ad_c, "D", "C"))
}

# Tone A trained alone under the adaptive model (Section 3.2): its value and
# associability after each of the earlier trials, k = 0, ..., n_first.
tone_alone <- function(s = default_settings) {
  run <- adaptive_simulate(make_trials("A", 1, s$n_first, "Earlier trials"), S = c(A = s$S),
                           alpha_init = c(A = s$alpha_init), eta = s$eta)
  data.frame(k = 0:s$n_first, V = run$V, alpha = run$alpha)
}


# The pear trials: each light alone, each trial followed by the pear

# One light trained alone on n pear trials, under the adaptive model or with a
# fixed learning rate ("rw"). Given rate, the fixed-rate learner uses that
# learning rate instead of beta. Returns one row per completed pear trial
# k = 0, ..., n: V and alpha are the values after k pear trials; error, rate
# and gain describe pear trial k + 1.
pear_light <- function(model, V_start, alpha_start, s, rate = NULL, n = s$n_pear) {
  design <- make_trials("L", 1, n, "Pear trials")
  if (model == "adaptive") {
    run <- adaptive_simulate(design, S = c(L = s$S), alpha_init = c(L = alpha_start),
                             eta = s$eta, V_init = c(L = V_start), cue_names = "L")
    V <- run$V
    alpha <- run$alpha
    rates <- s$S * alpha
  } else {
    fixed <- if (is.null(rate)) s$beta else rate
    run <- rw_simulate(design, beta = c(L = fixed), V_init = c(L = V_start), cue_names = "L")
    V <- run$V
    alpha <- rep(NA_real_, n + 1)
    rates <- rep(fixed, n + 1)
  }
  data.frame(k = 0:n, V = V, alpha = alpha, rate = rates,
             error = c(1 - V[-(n + 1)], NA), gain = c(diff(V), NA))
}

# Both models, both lights, on the pear trials under the settings in s. Each
# model's gap is the B-D gap, D's learned value for the pear minus B's, after
# k = 0, ..., n pear trials.
run_inquiry <- function(s = default_settings, n = s$n_pear) {
  st <- trained_states(s)
  rw <- st$rw
  ad <- st$adaptive

  # Associabilities at the start of the pear trials (Equation 4). Remove
  # resets both to alpha_init (Section 4.1).
  a_B <- s$alpha_init + s$g_alpha * (ad$alpha_B - s$alpha_init)
  a_D <- s$alpha_init + s$g_alpha * (ad$alpha_D - s$alpha_init)
  if (s$change == "remove") a_B <- a_D <- s$alpha_init

  # Learned values for the pear start at g_V times those for the apple (Equation 5).
  rw_B <- pear_light("rw", s$g_V * rw$V_B, NA, s, n = n)
  rw_D <- pear_light("rw", s$g_V * rw$V_D, NA, s, n = n)

  if (s$change == "supply") {
    # A Rescorla-Wagner learner that starts the pear trials where the adaptive
    # model starts: the same values and the learning rates S * alpha, which
    # then stay fixed. Each light is alone, so its shared error is its own
    # error, as in the adaptive model. Only the change in associability
    # differs.
    ad_B <- pear_light("rw", s$g_V * ad$V_B, NA, s, rate = s$S * a_B, n = n)
    ad_D <- pear_light("rw", s$g_V * ad$V_D, NA, s, rate = s$S * a_D, n = n)
  } else {
    ad_B <- pear_light("adaptive", s$g_V * ad$V_B, a_B, s, n = n)
    ad_D <- pear_light("adaptive", s$g_V * ad$V_D, a_D, s, n = n)
  }

  list(settings = s, trained = st,
       start = list(alpha_B = a_B, alpha_D = a_D),
       rw = list(B = rw_B, D = rw_D, gap = rw_D$V - rw_B$V),
       adaptive = list(B = ad_B, D = ad_D, gap = ad_D$V - ad_B$V))
}

# Both models, both lights, when training continues with the apple (Step 2):
# each light alone, starting from the values and associabilities that the
# compound trials left. Returns the same structure as run_inquiry().
continue_apple <- function(s = default_settings) {
  st <- trained_states(s)
  rw <- st$rw
  ad <- st$adaptive
  rw_B <- pear_light("rw", rw$V_B, NA, s)
  rw_D <- pear_light("rw", rw$V_D, NA, s)
  ad_B <- pear_light("adaptive", ad$V_B, ad$alpha_B, s)
  ad_D <- pear_light("adaptive", ad$V_D, ad$alpha_D, s)
  list(settings = s, trained = st,
       start = list(alpha_B = ad$alpha_B, alpha_D = ad$alpha_D),
       rw = list(B = rw_B, D = rw_D, gap = rw_D$V - rw_B$V),
       adaptive = list(B = ad_B, D = ad_D, gap = ad_D$V - ad_B$V))
}

# Each model's gap after k pear trials as the carryover of learned value
# varies, with g_alpha as in s (Figure 5a).
gap_by_value_carryover <- function(k = 8, g_V = seq(0, 1, by = .01), s = default_settings) {
  rows <- lapply(g_V, function(g) {
    r <- run_inquiry(modifyList(s, list(g_V = g)))
    c(g_V = g, rw = r$rw$gap[k + 1], adaptive = r$adaptive$gap[k + 1])
  })
  as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, rows))
}


# Section 4.4: the rank-based rule (Supplement S3)

# Associability moves the fraction step of the way toward 1 when a cue makes
# the smaller error and toward 0 when it makes the larger error. Errors closer
# than the square root of the machine precision count as equal. Equal errors
# leave associability unchanged or, with ties_lower = TRUE, lower it as a
# larger error does. Learned values change as in Equation 2. Each trial in
# trials gives the cues present; every trial is followed by its outcome.
rank_run <- function(trials, V, alpha, S, step, ties_lower = FALSE) {
  tolerance <- sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)
  for (cues in trials) {
    V_start <- V
    for (i in cues) V[i] <- V[i] + S[i] * alpha[i] * (1 - V_start[i])
    for (i in cues) {
      e_own <- abs(1 - V_start[i])
      e_other <- abs(1 - sum(V_start[setdiff(cues, i)]))
      alpha[i] <- if (e_own + tolerance < e_other) {
        alpha[i] + step * (1 - alpha[i])
      } else if (e_other + tolerance < e_own || ties_lower) {
        alpha[i] * (1 - step)
      } else {
        alpha[i]
      }
    }
  }
  list(V = V, alpha = alpha)
}

# The step that leaves B, after the compound trials, at the associability that
# Equation 3 gives it. B makes the larger error on every compound trial, so
# its associability is multiplied by 1 - step on each of them.
rank_step <- function(s = default_settings) {
  1 - (trained_states(s)$adaptive$alpha_B / s$alpha_init)^(1 / s$n_compound)
}

# D's associability after the compound trials, and the B-D gap over n pear
# trials, under a rule for associability: "proportional" (Equation 3),
# "rank" (rank-based, ties leave associability unchanged) or "rank_ties"
# (rank-based, ties lower it). Tone C's salience is S * (1 + c_offset).
# Learned values for the pear start at zero, and associability carries over in
# full.
rule_comparison <- function(rule = c("proportional", "rank", "rank_ties"), c_offset = 0,
                            s = default_settings, n = 15) {
  rule <- match.arg(rule)
  if (rule == "proportional") {
    r <- run_inquiry(modifyList(s, list(c_offset = c_offset, g_V = 0, g_alpha = 1,
                                        change = "none")), n = n)
    return(list(alpha_B = r$start$alpha_B, alpha_D = r$start$alpha_D, gap = r$adaptive$gap))
  }
  ties <- rule == "rank_ties"
  step <- rank_step(s)
  history <- function(first, pair, S) {
    cues <- unique(c(first, pair))
    state <- rank_run(rep(list(first), s$n_first), setNames(rep(0, length(cues)), cues),
                      setNames(rep(s$alpha_init, length(cues)), cues), S, step, ties)
    rank_run(rep(list(pair), s$n_compound), state$V, state$alpha, S, step, ties)
  }
  pear <- function(alpha_start) {
    state <- list(V = c(L = 0), alpha = c(L = alpha_start))
    values <- 0
    for (m in seq_len(n)) {
      state <- rank_run(list("L"), state$V, state$alpha, c(L = s$S), step, ties)
      values <- c(values, state$V[["L"]])
    }
    values
  }
  S_all <- c(A = s$S, B = s$S, X = s$S, C = s$S * (1 + c_offset), D = s$S)
  alpha_B <- history("A", c("A", "B"), S_all)$alpha[["B"]]
  alpha_D <- history("X", c("C", "D"), S_all)$alpha[["D"]]
  list(alpha_B = alpha_B, alpha_D = alpha_D, gap = pear(alpha_D) - pear(alpha_B))
}


# Section 5: from learned value to a yes response

# The sigmoid of Equation 7, with slope gamma and midpoint theta, and the
# threshold rule, which gives a yes whenever the learned value exceeds theta.
response_prob <- function(V, rule = c("sigmoid", "threshold"), gamma = 8, theta = .5) {
  rule <- match.arg(rule)
  if (rule == "sigmoid") obs_sigmoid(V, gamma = gamma, theta = theta)
  else obs_threshold(V, theta = theta)
}


# The decision model of Step 7
#
# A drift diffusion model with noise standard deviation 1, boundaries at 0 and
# a, start at a/2, and no deadline. The accuracy (Equation 9) and the mean
# decision time have closed forms. The density of the decision time uses the
# large-time series of Navarro and Fuss (2009), as in Figure 10c, and the
# percentage of decisions finished by each time is that density summed by the
# trapezoid rule.

ddm_settings <- data.frame(id = c("first", "second"), v = c(.30, .60), a = c(2.0, 1.0))

ddm_acc <- function(v, a) 1 / (1 + exp(-v * a))                  # Equation 9
ddm_mean <- function(v, a) a / (2 * v) * tanh(v * a / 2)         # mean decision time
# Density at the lower boundary, with the start at w * a and K terms of the series.
ddm_dens_lower <- function(t, v, a, w = .5, K = 300) {
  k <- seq_len(K)
  vapply(t, function(tt) {
    if (tt <= 0) return(0)
    (pi / a^2) * exp(-v * a * w - v^2 * tt / 2) *
      sum(k * exp(-k^2 * pi^2 * tt / (2 * a^2)) * sin(k * pi * w))
  }, numeric(1))
}
# Both boundaries together: the upper boundary (the correct response) uses -v
# and 1 - w, which is also .5.
ddm_dens <- function(t, v, a) ddm_dens_lower(t, v, a) + ddm_dens_lower(t, -v, a)
# The proportion of decisions finished by each time in times, which must start
# at 0 and be evenly spaced.
ddm_finished <- function(times, v, a) {
  f <- ddm_dens(times, v, a)
  c(0, cumsum((head(f, -1) + f[-1]) / 2 * diff(times)))
}

ddm_summary <- function() {
  d <- ddm_settings
  d$acc <- ddm_acc(d$v, d$a)
  d$mean <- ddm_mean(d$v, d$a)
  # Finished by time 0.5, on the grid of .0005 used for Figure 10c.
  d$by_half <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), function(i)
    tail(ddm_finished(seq(0, .5, by = .0005), d$v[i], d$a[i]), 1), numeric(1))
  d
}
