The responses and every # analysis come from data/inference_cases.rds, written by # shiny_app/make_inference_cases.R from the paper's simulation study. Nothing # is fitted here. Which process generated the case is revealed in Step 6. experiment_ui <- function() scene("scene-5", "5", "What an experiment could establish", "output.done_q4c", "done_e4", "Detecting a B–D difference was easier than identifying its source. How often the comparison favors the right explanation depends on the number of participants and on which responses are analyzed.", p("So far we worked with the models directly. In an experiment, we have only the responses, and we must infer which choices would give predictions that match them. Several combinations of choices can lead to similar predicted responses, so the inference can leave some choices undetermined. Before collecting data, we can ask how much a proposed experiment and its analysis could establish."), p("In a simulated experiment, a model generates the responses that the proposed experiment might produce, and we analyze them as if we did not know which process generated them. We can then check whether the analysis gives the right conclusion under the conditions we specify, although not whether those conditions describe real learners."), h3("The simulated experiment"), P("Each simulated participant completes the training of Step 2 and then the pear trials, answering on each pear trial, before the pear appears, whether they expect the pear. Each participant thus gives ten responses to ", B_gloss, " and ten to ", D_gloss, ". B and D are training roles, and either of the two physical lights can fill either role."), p("Each response is drawn as yes with the probability that a sigmoid gives for the light's current learned value, and as no otherwise. The simulated participants also differ in how fast they learn. Each is one of two types, with larger or smaller learning rates, and keeps that type throughout. The two physical lights may differ in how noticeable they are, so they are counterbalanced. Each serves as B for half the participants and as D for the other half. Each light's ten pear trials form one block, and half of each group sees the D block first."), experiment_formula_ui(), h3("Choose a case and design the experiment"), p("Each case is a set of simulated participants whose responses were generated by one process. You will learn which process at the end of Step 6, after analyzing the responses. Choose any case."), uiOutput("e_case"), p("Then choose how many participants to test and which responses to analyze. Every participant completes all ten pear trials with each light, and the models process every trial. Only the responses used in the analysis change."), p(class = "muted", "The 40-person and 160-person samples are separate simulated experiments. Within a case and sample size, changing the analyzed pear trials keeps the same participants and their responses."), div(class = "question", uiOutput("e_design")), conditionalPanel("output.done_e_design", h3("Detecting a difference"), uiOutput("e_design_line"), fig("e_records", "330px"), p(class = "table-note", "The grid shows the first 24 participants. A row follows the same person in both panels. Colored cells are yes, gray cells are no, and blank cells are not analyzed. The analyses use everyone in your sample."), p("For each participant, we calculate the proportion of yes responses to D minus the proportion to B, over the analyzed pear trials. Six yes responses to D and two to B, out of ten each, give a difference of (6 − 2)/10 = .40."), fig("e_participants", "340px"), p(class = "table-note", "Each dot is one participant. The colors show the two counterbalancing groups: in one, light 1 served as B, and in the other, light 2. To summarize the difference, we average it within each group and give the groups equal weight, so that a difference between the physical lights does not favor B or D. The interval comes from how much the participants' differences vary, so it does not treat a participant's responses as independent."), uiOutput("e_effect"), div(class = "question", uiOutput("e1")), conditionalPanel("output.done_e1", div(class = "question", uiOutput("e2"))), conditionalPanel("output.done_e2", fig("e_contrast", "260px"), p(class = "table-note", "Points show the difference in the proportion of yes responses, D minus B, on each analyzed pear trial, with approximate 95% intervals for paired proportions."), uiOutput("e_contrast_text"), h3("Comparing explanations by predicting new participants"), p("To choose among explanations, we compare three candidates built from the two learning models. All three are fitted to the responses with the same response function for both lights, and all three can also carry over learned value from the apple, with the fraction estimated from the responses."), tags$table(class = "values two", tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th("Candidate"), tags$th("Learning rule"), tags$th("Associability carried into the pear trials"))), tags$tbody( vrow("Carryover", "Adaptive model", paste0("An estimated fraction of the earlier change, ", gA)), vrow("Reset", "Adaptive model", "None, but associability still changes during the pear trials"), vrow("Fixed-rate", RW, "No changing associability: learning rates stay fixed across trials"))), p(class = "table-note", HTML("Each candidate also estimates the carryover of learned value, a baseline learning rate and the difference between faster and slower participants, the salience difference between the physical lights, and the intercept and slope of the response function. The carryover and reset candidates also estimate η.")), p("The fixed-rate and reset candidates can therefore explain a B–D difference through carried-over learned value. The reset candidate is the adaptive model with Remove from Step 3."), p("Each candidate is fitted by finding the parameter values under which the observed responses are most probable. To compare the candidates, we ask how well each predicts participants whose responses were not used for fitting. The participants are split into two halves, with equal numbers from each counterbalancing group. Each candidate is fitted to one half and scores its predictions for the other, and then the halves swap. This is called two-fold cross-validation."), p("Each prediction is scored by the logarithm of the probability it gave to the response that occurred, the log score. A prediction of .8 for yes scores log .8 if the response is yes and log .2 if it is no, so a confident prediction that turns out wrong is penalized heavily. The scores are summed over the held-out participants, and a higher total means better prediction."), p("To decide when an advantage is large enough, we use a rule fixed before the study. For the carryover candidate and each alternative, we take the difference in held-out log score and its standard error, calculated from the spread of the participants' score differences. Twice that standard error is the decision margin. Associability carryover is favored if the carryover candidate beats both alternatives by more than their margins. A candidate without associability carryover is favored if either alternative beats the carryover candidate by more than its margin. Otherwise the comparison is unresolved. This is a practical rule for classifying simulated experiments, not a calibrated significance test or the probability that an explanation is true."), tags$details(class = "formula-details", tags$summary("The terms in plain language"), tags$table(class = "values two", tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th("Term"), tags$th("What it means"))), tags$tbody( vrow("Likelihood", "The probability of the observed responses under a candidate with particular parameter values. Fitting chooses the values that make it highest (maximum likelihood estimation)."), vrow("Log score", "The logarithm of the probability that a prediction gave to the response that occurred. Better predictions score closer to zero."), vrow("Cross-validation", "Fitting a candidate to some participants and scoring its predictions for the others."), vrow("Decision margin", "Twice the standard error of the difference between two candidates' held-out log scores. A candidate is favored only if its advantage is larger than this margin.")))), div(class = "question", uiOutput("e3"))), conditionalPanel("output.done_e3", fig("e_scores", "170px"), p(class = "muted", "Bars show two standard errors either side. Associability carryover is favored when both bars lie entirely to the right of 0, and a candidate without it when a bar lies entirely to the left of 0. Otherwise the comparison is unresolved."), uiOutput("e_scores_text"), tags$details(class = "formula-details", tags$summary("What a preferred candidate can leave uncertain"), P("Even when the carryover candidate is favored, some of its parameters may be poorly determined. B's associability at the start of the pear trials depends on how far it fell during the compound trials and on how much of that fall carried over, ", gA, ". How far it fell is set partly by η. A fall from .500 to ", num(trained$adaptive$alpha_B), ", half of which carries over, leaves B at about ", num(ga_half$start$alpha_B), ". A smaller fall to ", num(ga_half$start$alpha_B), ", carried over in full, leaves B at the same value. This is a problem of parameter identifiability. In the tutorial's worked example, values of ", gA, " from .5 to 1 fitted the responses almost equally well, because η could make up for carrying over less of the fall."), p("Different models might also fit the same responses. The extent to which one model can reproduce another's predictions after adjusting its parameters is called model mimicry. The fixed-rate and reset candidates can imitate the later part of the B–D difference that the adaptive model predicts, by carrying over learned value for the apple. But carried-over value also gives them a difference before much learning has occurred, so over all ten pear trials, much of their discrepancy from the adaptive model's predictions lies in the first pear trials. On pear trials 8–10 alone, they come very close to those predictions."), aside("Section 6.4.")), h3("How reliable the planned analysis would be"), p("The result of one simulated experiment depends on the particular responses drawn. The tutorial therefore simulated 400 experiments for each generating process and sample size, analyzed each with the same candidates and decision rule, and repeated the analysis on pear trials 1–6 and on pear trials 8–10 of the same responses. The processes were:"), tags$ul( tags$li("Carried associability, the process the carryover candidate represents: the compound trials change associability, and part of that change carries over to the pear trials."), tags$li("Carried learned value, which the fixed-rate candidate can represent: learning rates stay fixed, and a B–D difference arises because learned values for the apple carry over. Favoring associability carryover would be a mistake here."), tags$li("Reset associability, the process the reset candidate represents: associability can change during the pear trials, but nothing that changed during the compound trials carries over, so there is no systematic B–D difference to find.")), div(class = "question", uiOutput("e4")), conditionalPanel("output.done_e4", uiOutput("e_rates"), settled("With enough participants, the planned analysis detected a difference generated by carried associability in nearly every experiment but favored associability carryover far less often. Under these conditions, we learn more from responses on all ten pear trials than from a larger final test.", "If all the candidates share a mistaken assumption, for example about the starting values or the response function, choosing the best of them cannot test it. Step 6 examines such an assumption."), aside("Section 6, Tables 7 to 9, Figures 7 and 8 and Box 5.")))) ) experiment_server <- function(input, output, answers, add_note, flag) { # The design output$e_case <- renderUI({ a <- answers$e_design if (is.null(a)) radioButtons("e_design_set", span(class = "visually-hidden", "Case to examine"), inline = TRUE, choiceNames = unname(set_labels), choiceValues = names(set_labels), selected = "value") else p(span(class = "answered-label", "Case examined"), set_labels[[a$set]]) }) rec_choices <- c( late = "The responses on pear trials 8–10, as a final test might record.", early = "The responses on pear trials 1–6, when the difference emerges.", full = "The responses on all ten pear trials.") design_items <- list( item("n", "How many participants?", c(`40` = "40", `160` = "160")), item("rec", "Which responses are analyzed?", rec_choices)) ask_server("e_design", input, output, answers, design_items, reason = "Why these responses? Say what you hope they will tell you.", reason_required = TRUE, button = "Run the experiment", on_submit = function(a) { a$set <- input$e_design_set if (is.null(a$set) || !(a$set %in% names(set_labels))) a$set <- "value" answers$e_design <- a add_note("Step 5", "Design", "How many participants, and which responses are analyzed?", paste0(set_labels[[a$set]], ", ", a$n, " participants, ", view_labels[[a$rec]], " analyzed. Reason: ", a$reason), settings = design_set(a)) }) design_set <- function(a = answers$e_design) { cs <- cases[[a$set]][[a$n]] paste0(set_labels[[a$set]], ", ", a$n, " participants, ", view_labels[[a$rec]], " analyzed; dataset ID = ", cs$id, "; seed = ", cs$seed, "; parameter set = ", cs$config, "; earlier trials: 10 A+ and 10 X+ with the apple; compound trials: 10 AB+ and 10 CD+", " with the apple; pear trials: 10 with B alone and 10 with D alone, block order", " counterbalanced; physical lights counterbalanced equally", "; p(yes) = logistic(b + gamma * V), each response drawn as yes with that probability", "; b and gamma estimated in every candidate; candidates: fixed-rate (Rescorla–Wagner),", " reset and carryover (adaptive model), each estimating g_V", "; two-fold cross-validation with the held-out log score; carryover favored if both score", " differences exceed 2 SE, another candidate favored if either is below -2 SE, otherwise unresolved", "; mean difference: equal-weight average of the two counterbalancing groups, 95% t interval", " with Welch–Satterthwaite degrees of freedom; per-trial intervals: Agresti–Min for paired proportions") } case <- reactive({ a <- answers$e_design; req(a); cases[[a$set]][[a$n]] }) design <- reactive({ a <- answers$e_design; req(a); case()$designs[[a$rec]] }) output$e_design_line <- renderUI({ a <- answers$e_design; req(a) P("", set_labels[[a$set]], ", ", a$n, " participants, ", view_labels[[a$rec]], " analyzed.") }) output$e_records <- renderPlot(plot_records(case(), cols = design()$cols)) output$e_participants <- renderPlot(plot_participants(case(), design())) effect_text <- function() { e <- design()$effect d <- participant_differences(case(), design()$cols) paste0("For your ", case()$n, " participants and the pear trials you kept, the mean difference in the proportion of yes responses, D minus B, is ", num(e[["estimate"]]), " (95% interval ", num(e[["lower"]]), " to ", num(e[["upper"]]), "). Of the ", nrow(d), " participants, ", sum(d$difference <= 0), " gave D no more yes responses than B. In the group where light 1 served as B, the mean difference is ", num(mean(d$difference[d$group == 1])), ", and where light 2 served as B it is ", num(mean(d$difference[d$group == -1])), ".", if (e[["detected"]] == 1) " The interval lies above zero, so a positive B–D difference is detected in this sample." else if (e[["upper"]] < 0) " The interval lies below zero, so it gives no support for a positive B–D difference." else " The interval includes zero, so a positive B–D difference is not detected in this sample.") } output$e_effect <- renderUI(p(effect_text())) # What the responses show e1_choices <- c( more = "The mean D-minus-B difference is positive, with a 95% interval above zero.", none = "The 95% interval does not lie above zero, so a positive difference is not detected.", assoc = "B carried a lower associability into the pear trials.", value = "Learned values for the apple carried over to the pear.") e1_items <- list(item("e", "What do these responses show?", e1_choices)) ask_server("e1", input, output, answers, e1_items, feedback = function(a) { e <- design()$effect tagList( p(if (a$e %in% c("assoc", "value")) "The responses show only whether yes responses differ between B and D. Associability and learned value are explanations to compare, and more than one process can produce the same difference." else if (a$e == "more" && e[["detected"]] != 1) "A positive difference needs the whole interval to lie above zero, and this interval does not." else if (a$e == "none" && e[["detected"]] == 1) "The whole interval lies above zero, so a positive difference is detected. That supports a response difference but does not identify its source." else "Your reading matches the interval. What could have produced this pattern?")) }, on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 5", "Detecting a difference", "What do these responses show?", e1_choices[[a$e]], result = effect_text(), settings = design_set())) # Box 5: what produced the difference? est_choices <- c(yes = "Yes. Only a lower associability for B makes D get more yes responses.", no = "No. Learned values for the apple carried over to the pear could also produce it.") look_choices <- c(first = "The responses on the first pear trial with each light.", last = "The responses on the last pear trials.", overall = "The overall proportion of yes responses.") e2_items <- list( item("est", "Suppose the participants answered yes more often to D than to B. Does this establish that B carried a lower associability into the pear trials?", est_choices), item("look", "What in the sequence of responses could show whether the difference was present from the start or developed during the pear trials?", look_choices)) e2_text <- "A B–D difference could arise because learned values for the apple carry over or because the lights carry over different associabilities (Step 3). With a shared response function, only carried-over learned value can make the first-response probabilities differ (Step 4). The mean difference averages over the pear trials, whereas the responses on each pear trial show when the difference appears." ask_server("e2", input, output, answers, e2_items, button = "See the responses on each pear trial", feedback = function(a) tagList( if (a$est == "yes") p("A difference in responses does not show where it came from. Step 3 showed that carried-over learned value can also put D ahead of B."), if (a$look != "first") p(if (a$look == "last") "By the last pear trials both kinds of gap can look alike. The first pear trial is where they differ most clearly." else "The overall proportion mixes all the pear trials, so it cannot show when the difference appeared."), p(e2_text)), on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 5", "What produced the difference?", e2_items[[1]]$label, paste0(est_choices[[a$est]], " To look at: ", look_choices[[a$look]]), result = e2_text, settings = design_set())) output$e_contrast <- renderPlot({ req(answers$e2); plot_contrast(case(), design()) }) output$e_contrast_text <- renderUI({ req(answers$e2) d <- design() if (!(1 %in% d$cols)) return(P("Your analysis kept pear trials ", min(d$cols), "–", max(d$cols), ", so it cannot show whether the difference was present on the first pear trial.")) first <- d$by_trial[d$by_trial$trial == 1, ] P("On the first pear trial, the observed difference is ", num(first$estimate), " (approximate 95% interval ", num(first$lower), " to ", num(first$upper), "). ", if (first$lower > 0) "This interval lies above zero, so the first responses already differ. Step 6 tests them with an exact paired test." else "This interval includes zero. Step 6 tests the first responses with an exact paired test.") }) # The comparison of the candidates e3_choices <- c( process = "That B carried a lower associability into the pear trials in these participants.", best = "That, among these three candidates, the carryover candidate predicts new participants best.") e3_items <- list(item("pref", "Before you see the comparison: if the carryover candidate predicted held-out participants better than both alternatives by more than the decision margins, what would that show?", e3_choices)) e3_text <- "A preference applies only to the candidates that were compared. The scores measure how well these candidates predict participants whose responses were held out. Whether one of them captures the process that produced the responses is a separate question, which Step 6 takes up." ask_server("e3", input, output, answers, e3_items, button = "Run the comparison", feedback = function(a) tagList( if (a$pref == "process") p("A candidate can win this comparison while sharing a mistaken assumption with every alternative, and the process that generated the responses may be missing from the candidates."), p(e3_text)), on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 5", "What a preference would show", e3_items[[1]]$label, e3_choices[[a$pref]], result = paste0(e3_text, " ", score_sentence("estimated")), settings = paste0(design_set(), "; ", policy_label[["estimated"]]))) # Score differences and their standard errors to one decimal; where both are # below .05, to two significant digits, so that the decision can be checked # from the printed numbers. score_num <- function(x, difference, se) { if (abs(difference) >= .05 || se >= .05) num0(x, 1) else if (x == 0) "0" else formatC(x, digits = 2, format = "fg", flag = "#") } score_sentence <- function(policy) { d <- design(); scores <- d$scores[[policy]] f <- scores[scores$against == "fixed", ]; r <- scores[scores$against == "reset", ] bar <- function(s) paste0(score_num(s$difference, s$difference, s$se), ", SE ", score_num(s$se, s$difference, s$se), ", so the bar runs from ", score_num(s$difference - 2 * s$se, s$difference, s$se), " to ", score_num(s$difference + 2 * s$se, s$difference, s$se)) paste0("Carryover minus fixed-rate: ", bar(f), ". Carryover minus reset: ", bar(r), ". Under the decision rule, the comparison ", decision_text[[d$decision[[policy]]]], ".", if (near_reset_scores(scores)) " The carryover and reset candidates have nearly identical held-out scores. A difference this small can still meet the rule, and it does not show how precisely carryover was estimated.") } output$e_scores <- renderPlot({ req(answers$e3); plot_scores(design()$scores$estimated) }) output$e_scores_text <- renderUI({ req(answers$e3); p(score_sentence("estimated")) }) # The repeated experiments rates_for <- function(source, n, view) rates[rates$scenario == source & rates$n == n & rates$view == view, ] output$e_rates <- renderUI({ req(answers$e3) a <- answers$e_design # One row of percentages; with design = TRUE it also names the design, and # the reader's own design is marked. row <- function(src, n, view, design = FALSE) { r <- rates_for(src, n, view) mine <- design && n == as.integer(a$n) && view == a$rec tags$tr(class = if (mine) "mine", tags$td(class = "nowrap", process_names[[src]]), if (design) tagList(tags$td(class = "nowrap", paste0(view_labels[[view]], if (mine) " (yours)")), tags$td(n)), tags$td(pct(r$detected)), tags$td(pct(r$carry)), tags$td(pct(r$unresolved)), tags$td(pct(r$no_carry))) } heads <- function(full) tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th("Responses generated by"), if (full) tagList(tags$th("Pear trials"), tags$th("N")), tags$th("Detected"), tags$th("Carryover favored"), tags$th("Unresolved"), tags$th("Fixed-rate or reset favored"))) sources <- c("associability", "value", "reset") tagList( P("For your design, ", a$n, " participants with ", view_labels[[a$rec]], " analyzed, the percentages of the 400 experiments per process were:"), div(class = "scroll-x", tabindex = "0", role = "region", `aria-label` = "Results for your design", tags$table(class = "values rates", heads(FALSE), tags$tbody(lapply(sources, function(src) row(src, as.integer(a$n), a$rec))))), p(class = "table-note", "Detected: the 95% interval for the mean difference lies above zero. The last three columns give the decision of the comparison and add to 100% apart from rounding. Favoring associability carryover is correct only for responses generated by carried associability. Each row averages, with equal weight, four parameter sets: combinations of settings such as how fast the participants learn and how steep the response function is. It therefore describes a broader range of conditions than your case, which uses the base parameter set."), P("Your experiment ", if (design()$effect[["detected"]] == 1) "detected" else "did not detect", " a positive difference, and its comparison ", decision_text[[design()$decision$estimated]], "."), tags$details(class = "formula-details", tags$summary("All six designs"), div(class = "scroll-x", tabindex = "0", role = "region", `aria-label` = "All designs", tags$table(class = "values rates", heads(TRUE), tags$tbody(unlist(lapply(sources, function(src) lapply(c(160L, 40L), function(n) lapply(c("full", "early", "late"), function(view) row(src, n, view, design = TRUE)))), recursive = FALSE)))), p(class = "table-note", "Supplementary Table S2 of the tutorial reports the same percentages."))) }) e4_choices <- c(detect = "Detecting a B–D difference.", identify = "Identifying that it came from carried associability.", same = "Both are about equally easy.") e4_items <- list(item("which", "With your design, which is easier when the responses were generated by carried associability?", e4_choices)) e4_text <- function() { a <- answers$e_design mine <- rates_for("associability", as.integer(a$n), a$rec) full <- rates_for("associability", 160L, "full") late <- rates_for("associability", 160L, "late") small <- rates_for("associability", 40L, "full") paste0("With your design, a positive difference generated by carried associability is detected in ", pct(mine$detected), " of the experiments, but associability carryover is favored in only ", pct(mine$carry), ".", if (!(a$n == "160" && a$rec == "full")) paste0(" With 160 participants and all ten pear trials, the percentages are ", pct(full$detected), " and ", pct(full$carry), "."), " With 160 participants and only pear trials 8–10, associability carryover is favored in ", pct(late$carry), ", and a candidate without it is wrongly favored in ", pct(late$no_carry), ", because by those trials the alternatives can imitate the generating process closely. With 40 participants and all ten pear trials, associability carryover is favored in ", pct(small$carry), ", more often than with 160 participants and pear trials 8–10, although 800 responses are analyzed against 960.") } ask_server("e4", input, output, answers, e4_items, feedback = function(a) tagList( if (a$which != "detect") p("Detecting a difference was the easier task under every design."), p(e4_text())), on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 5", "Detecting and identifying", e4_items[[1]]$label, e4_choices[[a$which]], result = e4_text(), settings = design_set(), open = "If all the candidates share a mistaken assumption, for example about the starting values or the response function, can choosing the best of them test it?")) # Trying another design or case, or starting the inquiry again, clears the # answers but keeps the notes. list(case = case, design = design, design_set = design_set, score_sentence = score_sentence, effect_text = effect_text, reset = function() clear_answers(answers, c("e_design", "e1", "e2", "e3", "e4"))) }

content: # Step 2: telling two explanations apart (Section 3) # The comparison light D with its new companion, the adaptive model and its # first compound trials, the states that both models leave, the choice of a # comparison, the pear trials (Box 2), and why the adaptive model's gap # narrows. explanations_ui <- function() { scene("scene-2", "2", "Telling two explanations apart", "output.done_q1c", "done_q2d", "Both models leave B below D. Only the adaptive model gives B a lower learning rate, and with the pear it predicts that B learns more slowly than D.", p("A light might learn less simply because it shares the apple with a companion, whether or not the companion was trained first. We therefore compare the light of Step 1 with a light whose companion is new. As with a control condition in an experiment, the two lights should then differ in one respect only."), h3("A light with a new companion"), p("We now need more letters, and they come in matching pairs: A and C are tones, and B and D are lights. (optional)", button = "See the pear trials", feedback = function(a) tagList(lapply(q2c_feedback(a), P)), on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 2", "What changes when the picture changes", "B and D start the pear trials at zero. How do their first gains compare under each model?", paste0(RW, ": ", first_choices[[a$rw]], " Adaptive model: ", first_choices[[a$ad]], " Reason: ", why_choices[[a$why]], if (nzchar(a$reason)) paste0(" You added: ", a$reason)), result = paste(q2c_feedback(a), collapse = " "), settings = first_set())) output$p2_curves <- renderPlot({ req(answers$q2c); plot_curves(base) }) output$p2_gap <- renderPlot({ req(answers$q2c); plot_gap(base, ylim = c(-.02, .32)) }) # One row per step of the calculation, so that the table reads top to bottom. output$trial_table <- renderUI({ req(answers$q2c, input$t_model, input$t_k) m <- input$t_model; j <- input$t_k B <- base[[m]]$B; D <- base[[m]]$D row <- function(label, f) tags$tr(tags$td(label), tags$td(f(B)), tags$td(f(D))) tagList(tags$table(class = "values", tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th(paste("Pear trial", j)), tags$th(class = "cue-B", "B"), tags$th(class = "cue-D", "D"))), tags$tbody( row("Value before", function(d) prob(at(d$V, j - 1))), row("Error", function(d) prob(at(d$error, j - 1))), row("Associability", function(d) if (m == "rw") "—" else num(at(d$alpha, j - 1))), row("Learning rate", function(d) num(at(d$rate, j - 1))), row("Gain", function(d) num(at(d$gain, j - 1))), row("Value after", function(d) num(at(d$V, j))))), p(class = "table-note", "Gains, values and gaps are calculated from unrounded values, so a hand calculation can differ in the last digit.")) }) output$trial_note <- renderUI({ req(answers$q2c, input$t_model, input$t_k) m <- input$t_model; j <- input$t_k gain_B <- at(base[[m]]$B$gain, j - 1); gain_D <- at(base[[m]]$D$gain, j - 1) p(class = "muted", paste0("Gap after pear trial ", j, ": ", prob(at(base[[m]]$gap, j)), ". ", if (m == "rw") "B and D gain the same." else if (gain_B > gain_D) "On this trial B gains more than D, so the gap narrows." else "On this trial D gains more than B, so the gap grows.")) }) # Why the adaptive model's gap narrows after its peak. q2d_choices <- c( stop = "D stops learning once its learned value is high enough, so only B keeps gaining.", converge = "B's associability catches up with D's, so B again learns as readily as D.", error = "B has more of the pear left to learn, and its larger error comes to outweigh its lower learning rate, so B starts to gain more per trial than D.", overtake = "B's learned value overtakes D's after the eighth pear trial.") q2d_items <- list(item("n", paste0("The adaptive model's gap is largest after ", pear_trials(peak_k), " and then narrows. Why?"), q2d_choices)) alpha_gap <- ad_D$alpha - ad_B$alpha narrow_text <- paste0("On the ", ordinal(peak_k + 1), " pear trial, B gains about ", num(at(ad_B$gain, peak_k)), " and D about ", num(at(ad_D$gain, peak_k)), ", so the gap begins to narrow, although D still has the higher value. At first D gains more because its learning rate is higher. As B falls behind, however, it has more of the pear left to learn, and so a larger error. Its associability is still the lower one: D's exceeds B's by ", num(at(alpha_gap, peak_k)), ", up from ", num(at(alpha_gap, 0)), " at the start of the pear trials. B can narrow the gap without overtaking D.") ask_server("q2d", input, output, answers, q2d_items, feedback = function(a) P(switch(a$n, stop = "D keeps learning on every pear trial. ", converge = "B's associability does rise during the pear trials, but D's rises faster. When a light is trained alone, a smaller error gives a larger increase in associability, and D predicts the pear more accurately than B. ", error = "", overtake = "B never overtakes D under these assumptions. The gap stays positive after every pear trial. What changes is how much each light gains per trial. "), narrow_text), on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 2", "Why the gap narrows", q2d_items[[1]]$label, q2d_choices[[a$n]], result = narrow_text, settings = first_set(), open = "Does the gap remain under other choices about carryover, training and the rule for associability?")) # Starting the inquiry again clears the answers and the comparisons tried but # keeps the notes. list(reset = function() { clear_answers(answers, c("q2a", "q2b", "q2c", "q2d")) cmp_tries(list()); cmp_picking(TRUE); cmp_msg(NULL) }) }

# Explore: change the settings freely
# The controls cover the changes to the adaptive model (Section 4.1), the
# carryover to the pear trials (4.2), the amount of training and the rate eta
# (4.3), the salience of the new tone C (4.4) and the response function
# (Section 5). Every curve is computed live with engine.R.

explore_ui <- function() div(class = "part wide",
  p(class = "lead",
    "Try changing the training, what carries over to the pear trials, or the response function.
     The curves update as you go. You start with the settings used in the inquiry and the
     tutorial."),
  p(class = "muted", HTML("B is the light that appeared with the trained tone A, and D is the
     comparison light, which appeared with the new tone C. Both are trained with the apple and
     then shown alone with the pear. A positive B–D gap means that D's learned value for
     the pear is higher than B's.")),
  p(class = "muted", "The saved cases of Steps 5 and 6 stay the same, and Explore settings are
     not added to your notes."),
  div(class = "explore",
    div(class = "explore-controls",
      div(class = "control-primary",
        h3("Change the adaptive model"),
        p(class = "muted", "In the adaptive model, a cue's learning rate is its salience times its
           associability. Salience is a fixed weight, and associability changes with experience.
           The gain on a trial is the learning rate times the cue's own error."),
        radioButtons("x_change", span(class = "visually-hidden", "Change the adaptive model"), choices = c(
          "Unchanged: the adaptive model as specified" = "none",
          "Prevent: hold associability fixed during the compound trials" = "prevent",
          "Remove: reset associability to .5 before the pear trials" = "remove",
          "Supply: fixed learning rates during the pear trials" = "supply")),
        uiOutput("x_change_hint"),
        p(class = "small-screen-note", tags$a(href = "#x_change_explanation", "Read about this change")),
        aside("Section 4.1 compares these interventions with no carryover of learned value (Figure 4).")),
      tags$details(class = "control-group", open = NA, `data-mobile-collapse` = "true",
        tags$summary("Training"),
        p(class = "muted", "Set how many compound trials each pair, AB and CD, has with the apple.
           The earlier A+ and X+ trials stay at ten each. The rate of change controls how
           strongly associability responds to the difference between the errors, wherever the
           chosen model lets it change."),
        sliderInput("x_n2", "Compound trials per pair", 1, 30, 10, step = 1, ticks = FALSE),
        sliderInput("x_eta", HTML("Rate of change of associability, η"), .01, .10, .05,
                    step = .01, ticks = FALSE)),
      tags$details(class = "control-group", open = NA, `data-mobile-collapse` = "true",
        tags$summary("Carryover to the pear trials"),
        p(class = "muted", "For learned value, 0 starts both lights at zero, and 1 keeps each
           light's full value for the apple. For associability, 0 resets both lights to .5, and
           1 keeps the associability reached at the end of the compound trials. Half carryover
           keeps half of the value, or half of the change in associability from .5. It does not
           halve associability itself."),
        sliderInput("x_gv", HTML(paste0("Learned value, ", gV)), 0, 1, 0, step = .05,
                    ticks = FALSE),
        sliderInput("x_ga", HTML(paste0("Associability, ", gA)), 0, 1, 1, step = .05,
                    ticks = FALSE)),
      tags$details(class = "control-group", id = "control-c",
        tags$summary("Salience of the new tone C"),
        p(class = "muted", "These settings change C's salience while keeping D's fixed. Explore
           uses the rule of Equation 3, under which a tiny difference in the errors gives a tiny
           change in associability, so the curves and rounded values may look the same. Step 3
           compares this rule with two rank-based rules."),
        radioButtons("x_c", span(class = "visually-hidden", "Salience of C relative to D"), choices = c(
          "Equal to D's" = "0",
          "One part in a million higher than D's" = "1e-6",
          "1% higher than D's" = "0.01",
          "1% lower than D's" = "-0.01"))),
      tags$details(class = "control-group",
        tags$summary("Response function"),
        p(class = "muted", "These settings affect only the plot of the difference in yes
           probability. The sigmoid rises gradually. Its midpoint gives a yes probability of .5,
           and a larger slope makes the rise steeper. The threshold rule gives a yes only above
           the threshold. Both lights use the same function."),
        radioButtons("x_rule", span(class = "visually-hidden", "Response function"), inline = TRUE,
                     choices = c("Sigmoid" = "sigmoid", "Threshold" = "threshold")),
        conditionalPanel("input.x_rule == 'sigmoid'",
          sliderInput("x_gamma", HTML("Slope, γ"), 1, 16, 8, step = .5, ticks = FALSE)),
        sliderInput("x_theta", HTML("Midpoint or threshold, θ"), 0, 1, .5, step = .05,
                    ticks = FALSE)),
      actionLink("x_reset", "Reset these settings")),
    div(class = "explore-output",
      uiOutput("x_change_explanation"),
      tags$details(class = "starting-states", id = "x_starting_states",
        tags$summary("Check the values and learning rates"),
        uiOutput("x_summary")),
      fig("x_curves", "300px"),
      fig("x_gap", "280px"),
      fig("x_resp", "280px"),
      h3("Pear trial by pear trial"),
      uiOutput("x_table_note"),
      div(class = "scroll-x", tabindex = "0", role = "region",
          `aria-label` = "Values after each pear trial", uiOutput("x_table"))))
)


explore_server <- function(input, output, session) {
  x_run <- reactive({
    req(input$x_n2, input$x_eta, !is.null(input$x_gv), !is.null(input$x_ga), input$x_change)
    run_inquiry(settings_with(
      n_compound = input$x_n2, eta = input$x_eta, g_V = input$x_gv,
      g_alpha = input$x_ga, change = input$x_change,
      c_offset = if (is.null(input$x_c)) 0 else as.numeric(input$x_c)))
  })
  x_label <- reactive(if (input$x_change == "supply") "Supply" else "Adaptive model")
  x_gamma <- reactive(if (is.null(input$x_gamma)) 8 else input$x_gamma)

  output$x_change_hint <- renderUI({
    req(input$x_change)
    p(class = "muted", switch(input$x_change,
      none = "Associability can change during the compound trials and the pear trials.",
      prevent = "Associability is held fixed during the compound trials only.",
      remove = "Both associabilities restart at .5 when the pear trials begin.",
      supply = "Each light keeps its starting learning rate throughout the pear trials. Its learned value still changes."))
  })
  output$x_change_explanation <- renderUI({
    req(input$x_change)
    div(class = "model-change-explanation",
      switch(input$x_change,
        none = tagList(
          h3("The adaptive model, unchanged"),
          p("During the compound trials, each cue's associability rises when it predicts the
             apple better than the cue presented with it and falls when it predicts worse, by an
             amount that grows with the difference between their errors. The carryover sliders
             set the values and associabilities that each light brings to the pear trials, where
             associability can change again."),
          p("Use these curves as a reference when you try one of the interventions. For a light
             trained alone, its error is compared with the error of predicting zero, so its
             associability can rise as it learns.")),
        prevent = tagList(
          h3("Prevent: hold associability fixed during the compound trials"),
          p("Each cue keeps the associability it had just before the AB+ and CD+ trials. B and D
             both start those trials at .5, so B cannot acquire a lower associability than D
             there. Their values for the apple still change. Associability can change again once
             the pear trials begin."),
          p("Does B's later disadvantage depend on an associability difference that develops
             during the compound trials?"),
          p(class = "muted", "This also changes what B learns about the apple. If you let
             learned value carry over, that difference enters the pear trials. The associability
             slider makes no difference to B and D here, because both leave the compound trials
             at .5.")),
        remove = tagList(
          h3("Remove: reset associability before the pear trials"),
          p("The compound trials run as usual, then B's and D's associabilities are reset to .5
             just before their first pear trial. Their learned values for the apple stay intact,
             and the learned-value slider still sets how much of them enters the pear trials.
             Associability can change again during the pear trials."),
          p("Does B's later disadvantage depend on keeping the associability difference from
             the compound trials? Here the difference is removed after it has formed, and the
             earlier learning about the apple is kept."),
          p(class = "muted", "While Remove is chosen, the associability slider has no effect:
             both lights restart at .5. Prevent changes the learning about the apple, and Remove
             changes associability only when the pear trials begin. With carried-over learned
             value, B therefore starts the pear trials at a different value under the two
             interventions.")),
        supply = {
          r <- x_run()
          tagList(
            h3(HTML(paste0("Supply: a ", RW, " learner with the adaptive model's learning rates"))),
            p("Each light starts the pear trials with the learned value and the learning rate it
               would have in the unchanged adaptive model, under your carryover settings. The
               learning rate then stays fixed throughout the pear trials. The learner still
               updates its learned value from its error on every trial."),
            P("B's fixed learning rate is ", num(at(r$adaptive$B$rate, 0)), ", and D's is ",
              num(at(r$adaptive$D$rate, 0)), ". Each is the light's salience times its
              associability in the adaptive model at the start of the pear trials. The separate ",
              RW, " curves keep their own starting values and learning rate."),
            p("How much of the B–D gap comes from the starting values and learning rates, and how
               much depends on associability continuing to change during the pear trials?"))
        }),
      if (input$x_change != "none") p(class = "muted", "In the gap plot, the pale line labeled
        “Unchanged” shows the unchanged adaptive model with the same slider settings."))
  })

  output$x_summary <- renderUI({
    r <- x_run(); end_apple <- r$trained$adaptive
    row <- function(label, B, D) tags$tr(tags$td(label), tags$td(prob(B)), tags$td(prob(D)))
    tagList(
      p("The first two rows show the adaptive model at the end of the compound trials. The
         others show the starting states for the pear trials."),
      div(class = "scroll-x", tabindex = "0", role = "region",
          `aria-label` = "Starting states", tags$table(class = "values",
        tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th(""), tags$th(class = "cue-B", "B"), tags$th(class = "cue-D", "D"))),
        tags$tbody(
          row("Learned value for the apple", end_apple$V_B, end_apple$V_D),
          row("Associability at the end of the compound trials", end_apple$alpha_B, end_apple$alpha_D),
          row("Learned value for the pear at the start", at(r$adaptive$B$V, 0), at(r$adaptive$D$V, 0)),
          if (input$x_change != "supply") row("Associability at the start of the pear trials",
                                              r$start$alpha_B, r$start$alpha_D),
          row(if (input$x_change == "supply") "Fixed learning rate during the pear trials"
              else "Learning rate on the first pear trial",
              at(r$adaptive$B$rate, 0), at(r$adaptive$D$rate, 0))))),
      P("Under ", RW, ", B starts the pear trials at ", prob(at(r$rw$B$V, 0)), " and D at ",
        prob(at(r$rw$D$V, 0)), ", with learning rate ", num(at(r$rw$B$rate, 0), 2),
        " for both lights."))
  })
  output$x_curves <- renderPlot(plot_curves(x_run(),
    labels = c(rw = "Rescorla–Wagner", adaptive = x_label())))
  # The unchanged adaptive model, drawn for reference when a change is chosen.
  x_ref <- reactive(if (input$x_change == "none") NULL else
    run_inquiry(modifyList(x_run()$settings, list(change = "none"))))
  # The axis always spans at least -.02 to .25, so a small gap looks small.
  output$x_gap <- renderPlot({
    r <- x_run()
    plot_gap(r, second = x_label(), ref = x_ref(),
             ylim = range(-.02, .25, r$rw$gap, r$adaptive$gap, x_ref()$adaptive$gap))
  })
  output$x_resp <- renderPlot(plot_response_models(x_run(), input$x_rule, x_gamma(),
                                                   input$x_theta, second = x_label()))
  output$x_table_note <- renderUI(p(class = "muted",
    if (input$x_change == "supply") "The last two columns show each light's fixed learning rate.
      The learning rates stay constant while the learned values change."
    else "Follow each light's learned value for the pear and its associability after every pear
      trial."))
  # Model names head pairs of B and D columns, so the table fits a narrow screen.
  # The third pair gives associability, or under Supply the fixed learning rate.
  output$x_table <- renderUI({
    r <- x_run()
    supply <- input$x_change == "supply"
    third <- if (supply) "rate" else "alpha"
    cues <- function() list(tags$th(class = "cue-B", "B"), tags$th(class = "cue-D", "D"))
    tags$table(class = "values grouped",
      tags$thead(
        tags$tr(tags$th(""), tags$th(colspan = 2, span(HTML(RW))),
                tags$th(colspan = 2, span(x_label())),
                tags$th(colspan = 2, span(if (supply) "Fixed learning rate" else "Associability"))),
        tags$tr(tags$th("After pear trial"), cues(), cues(), cues())),
      tags$tbody(lapply(1:10, function(k) tags$tr(tags$td(k),
        tags$td(num(at(r$rw$B$V, k))), tags$td(num(at(r$rw$D$V, k))),
        tags$td(num(at(r$adaptive$B$V, k))), tags$td(num(at(r$adaptive$D$V, k))),
        tags$td(num(at(r$adaptive$B[[third]], k))), tags$td(num(at(r$adaptive$D[[third]], k)))))))
  })

  explore_defaults <- function() {
    updateSliderInput(session, "x_n2", value = 10)
    updateSliderInput(session, "x_eta", value = .05)
    updateSliderInput(session, "x_gv", value = 0)
    updateSliderInput(session, "x_ga", value = 1)
    updateRadioButtons(session, "x_change", selected = "none")
    updateRadioButtons(session, "x_c", selected = "0")
    updateRadioButtons(session, "x_rule", selected = "sigmoid")
    updateSliderInput(session, "x_gamma", value = 8)
    updateSliderInput(session, "x_theta", value = .5)
  }
  observeEvent(input$x_reset, explore_defaults())
  list(defaults = explore_defaults)
}

content: # The model equations, with their symbols, numbered as in the paper. They are # written in MathML, which browsers display without an external typesetting # service. model_equation <- function(id, expression, number = NULL) div(class = "model-equation", id = id, HTML(paste0('', expression, '')), if (!is.null(number)) span(class = "equation-number", paste0("(", number, ")"))) # V_{i,t}, and the like, in MathML. mml_sub <- function(base, sub) paste0("", base, "", sub, "") mml_it <- "i,t" mml_next <- "i,t+1" # Step 1: Equation 1 rw_formula_ui <- function() tags$details(class = "formula-details", tags$summary("The rule as an equation"), P("Vi,t is the learned value of cue i, A or B, after t completed trials, and both cues start at zero. On trial t + 1, each cue present gets a new value:"), model_equation("formula-rw", paste0(' ', mml_sub("V", mml_next), '=', mml_sub("V", mml_it), '+', mml_sub("β", "i"), '(', mml_sub("λ", "t+1"), '−∑j∈', mml_sub("C", "t+1"), '', mml_sub("V", "j,t"), ')'), number = 1), P("Ct+1 is the set of cues present on the trial, and the sum is their combined prediction. The outcome λt+1 is 1 when the apple appears. The quantity in parentheses is the shared error. βi is cue i's fixed learning rate, here ", axis_num(default_settings$beta), " for both cues. The shared error is calculated before any cue changes value, and an absent cue keeps its value."), aside("Section 2.2, Equation 1.")) # Step 2: Equations 2 and 3 adaptive_formula_ui <- function() tags$details(class = "formula-details", tags$summary("The full rule as equations"), P("As in Step 1, t counts completed trials. For a cue i present on trial t + 1, the learned value changes by the cue's learning rate times its own error:"), model_equation("formula-adaptive", paste0(' ', mml_sub("V", mml_next), '=', mml_sub("V", mml_it), '+', mml_sub("β", mml_it), '(', mml_sub("λ", "t+1"), '−', mml_sub("V", mml_it), '),', mml_sub("β", mml_it), '=', mml_sub("S", "i"), mml_sub("α", mml_it), ''), number = 2), P("Si is the cue's salience, ", axis_num(default_settings$S), " for every cue, and αi,t its associability, which starts at ", axis_num(default_settings$alpha_init), ". Let ei,t+1 = |λt+1 − Vi,t| be the size of the cue's own error, and e−i,t+1 the size of the error made by the summed prediction of the other cues present. With one companion, this is the companion's error. For a cue presented alone, it is the error of predicting zero, |λt+1|. Then"), model_equation("formula-associability", paste0(' ', mml_sub("α", mml_next), '=', mml_sub("α", mml_it), '+η (', mml_sub("e", "−i,t+1"), '−', mml_sub("e", mml_next), ')'), number = 3), P("with η = ", axis_num(default_settings$eta), ". Associability is kept between .01 and 1: a value that would fall outside this range is set to the nearer bound. A cue that makes the larger error loses associability, and one that makes the smaller error gains it, by an amount proportional to the difference between the errors. Equal errors leave associability unchanged. Both updates use the values from before the trial, so a change in associability first affects learning on the next trial."), p("In R, the loop of Step 1 becomes:"), tags$pre(class = "code", "for (t in seq_along(design)) { cues <- design[[t]]$cues lambda <- design[[t]]$lambda e_own <- abs(lambda - V[cues]) e_other <- abs(lambda - (sum(V[cues]) - V[cues])) V[cues] <- V[cues] + S[cues] * alpha[cues] * (lambda - V[cues]) alpha[cues] <- alpha[cues] + eta * (e_other - e_own) alpha[cues] <- pmin(1, pmax(.01, alpha[cues])) }"), P("S[cues] * alpha[cues] is the learning rate. The value update uses each cue's own error, where the ", RW, " loop used the shared error. The order of the updates matters here: B must gain ", num(at(compound$B$ad_gain, 0)), " on its first compound trial, not the ", num(default_settings$S * at(compound$B$ad_alpha_after, 0)), " that its new associability of ", num(at(compound$B$ad_alpha_after, 0)), " would give."), aside("Section 3.3, Equations 2 and 3, and Table 2.")) # Step 3: Equations 4 and 5 carryover_formulas_ui <- function() tags$details(class = "formula-details", tags$summary("Both carryover fractions as equations"), model_equation("formula-associability-carryover", ' αi(0) =αinit+gα (αiend −αinit)', number = 4), model_equation("formula-value-carryover", ' Vi(0) =gV Viapple', number = 5), P("αiend is light i's associability at the end of the compound trials, αinit = ", axis_num(default_settings$alpha_init), " the associability with which every cue starts, and Viapple its learned value for the apple at the end of the compound trials. αi(0) is the light's associability, and Vi(0) its learned value for the pear, before its first pear trial. Both fractions lie between 0 and 1."), aside("Section 4.2, Equations 4 and 5.")) # Step 4: Equations 6 and 7, and the threshold rule response_formulas_ui <- function() tags$details(class = "formula-details", tags$summary("The response functions as equations"), P("Vi(k) is light i's learned value for the pear after k completed pear trials. The probability of a yes on the next pear trial is"), model_equation("formula-observation", ' pi(k)= f(Vi(k))', number = 6), P("where f is the response function. The sigmoid is"), model_equation("formula-sigmoid", ' f(V)= 11+exp[ −γ(V−θ)]', number = 7), P("θ is the learned value at which the probability of a yes is .5, and γ sets how steeply the probability rises around that value. Here γ = 8 and θ = .5. The threshold rule gives f(V) = 1 if V > θ and 0 otherwise, with θ = .5. Both functions are applied to B and D alike."), aside("Section 5, Equations 6 and 7.")) # Step 5: the response model of the simulated experiments experiment_formula_ui <- function() tags$details(class = "formula-details", tags$summary("How the simulated responses were generated"), P("The sigmoid of Step 4 is written with an intercept, b = −γθ, and a slope, γ. The probability of a yes at learned value V is then"), model_equation("formula-experiment-probability", ' 11+exp[−( b+γV )]'), P("Each response is drawn as yes with this probability, using the light's learned value after the participant's completed pear trials with it. The saved cases use the base parameter set of the tutorial: b = −4 and γ = 8, so the midpoint is .5, as in Step 4. Each participant is one of two learning-rate types, and a light starts with a learning rate of about .12 for the slower type and about .19 for the faster type, apart from the salience difference between the physical lights. There is no deadline."), model_equation("formula-ddm-accuracy", ' P(correct)= 11+exp(−va)', number = 9), model_equation("formula-ddm-time", ' E[Tdecision]= a2v tanh(va2)'), P("The second expression gives the probability of a correct response, and the third the mean decision time, correct and incorrect responses together. # Shared text, number formats and small building blocks # Names as the page writes them, in HTML. RW <- "Rescorla–Wagner" gV <- "gV" gA <- "gα" # B and D glossed, as at their first use in each step. B_gloss <- "B (the light that appeared with the trained tone)" D_gloss <- "D (the comparison light)" P <- function(...) p(HTML(paste0(...))) # a paragraph with simple markup fig <- function(id, height) div(class = "fig", plotOutput(id, height = height)) step_head <- function(n, title) h2(class = "step", span(class = "step-n", n), title) # One step of the inquiry, shown once the condition "show" holds. It is a #
element, so that a completed step can be folded and reopened. # "done" names the output that is TRUE once the step is complete; from then on # the heading also shows "summary", and a button leads to the next step. The # last step has no button. scene <- function(id, n, title, show, done, summary, ..., last = FALSE) { next_step <- as.integer(n) + 1L conditionalPanel(show, tags$details(id = id, class = "inquiry-scene", open = NA, `data-done` = done, tags$summary(step_head(n, title), p(class = "scene-summary", HTML(summary)), span(class = "scene-review", "Hide details")), div(class = "scene-content", ..., if (!last) conditionalPanel(paste0("output.", done), tags$button(type = "button", class = "btn-submit scene-continue", `data-next` = paste0("scene-", next_step), paste0("Continue to Step ", next_step)))))) } # Where the tutorial treats the same point, for readers who want more. aside <- function(...) p(class = "aside", HTML(paste0("In the tutorial: ", ...))) # What a step has settled and what it leaves open. settled <- function(settled_text, open_text) div(class = "settled", P("Settled. ", settled_text), P("Still open. ", open_text)) # num() drops the leading zero, as in the paper, for quantities that cannot # exceed 1. Like the paper, it rounds a value exactly halfway up (.2775 to # .278); the small offset keeps binary rounding error from turning such a value # down. num0() keeps the leading zero for quantities that can exceed 1 (times, # drift rates, log-score differences). Both print a negative value with a minus # sign rather than a hyphen, and a value that rounds to zero without a sign. num <- function(x, digits = 3) { s <- sub("^-(0[.]0*)$", "\\1", formatC(x + sign(x) * 1e-12, format = "f", digits = digits)) sub("^-", "\u2212", sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", s)) } num0 <- function(x, digits) sub("^-", "\u2212", sub("^-(0[.]0*)$", "\\1", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits))) p_text <- function(p) { if (p < .001) "p < .001" else if (p > .999) "p > .999" else paste("p =", num(p)) } # Axis labels and parameter values, without leading or trailing zeros: "0", # ".05", ".1". axis_num <- function(x) sub("^-", "\u2212", sub("^(-?)0[.]", "\\1.", format(x, trim = TRUE, drop0trailing = TRUE))) # Percentages to one decimal, as the paper's tables print them. pct <- function(x) paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = 1), "%") # Exact 0 and 1 (a zero gap, an error of 1, or the threshold rule's # probabilities) print as such. prob <- function(x, digits = 3) ifelse(x == 0 | abs(x) == 1, as.character(x), num(x, digits)) number_word <- function(k) c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten", "eleven", "twelve", "thirteen", "fourteen", "fifteen", "sixteen", "seventeen", "eighteen", "nineteen", "twenty")[k] pear_trials <- function(k) paste(number_word(k), if (k == 1) "pear trial" else "pear trials") ordinal <- function(k) c("first", "second", "third", "fourth", "fifth", "sixth", "seventh", "eighth", "ninth", "tenth", "eleventh", "twelfth", "thirteenth", "fourteenth", "fifteenth")[k] # Settings lines for the notes: the calculations of Steps 1 to 4 (without the # pear trials for results taken at the end of the compound trials). first_set <- function(s = default_settings, pear = TRUE) paste0( RW, ": shared error, learning rate ", axis_num(s$beta), "; adaptive model: own error, salience S = ", axis_num(s$S), ", starting associability ", axis_num(s$alpha_init), ", eta = ", axis_num(s$eta), "; learned values start at 0; apple and pear = 1; earlier trials: ", s$n_first, " A+ and ", s$n_first, " X+; compound trials: ", s$n_compound, " AB+ and ", s$n_compound, " CD+", if (pear) paste0("; pear trials: ", s$n_pear, " with B alone and ", s$n_pear, " with D alone; ", gV, " = ", axis_num(s$g_V), ", ", gA, " = ", axis_num(s$g_alpha)), "; salience of C = S * (1 + ", format(s$c_offset, scientific = s$c_offset != 0), "); change to the adaptive model: ", s$change) rule_set <- function(rule) if (rule == "sigmoid") "sigmoid, γ = 8, θ = .5" else "threshold, θ = .5" # The two training histories (Table 1); with pear = TRUE, also the pear # trials that Step 2 adds. design_table <- function(pear = FALSE) { tags$table(class = "design", tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th("History"), tags$th("Earlier trials"), tags$th("Compound trials"), if (pear) tags$th("Pear trials"))), tags$tbody( tags$tr(tags$td("Trained tone"), tags$td("10 A+"), tags$td("10 AB+"), if (pear) tags$td(class = "cue-B", "10 B alone")), tags$tr(tags$td("New tone"), tags$td("10 X+"), tags$td("10 CD+"), if (pear) tags$td(class = "cue-D", "10 D alone")))) } # A table row whose cells may contain simple markup, and a table header that # ends with B and D columns. vrow <- function(...) tags$tr(lapply(list(...), function(x) tags$td(HTML(x)))) cue_head <- function(...) tags$thead(tags$tr(lapply(list(...), tags$th), tags$th(class = "cue-B", "B"), tags$th(class = "cue-D", "D"))) # Steps 5 and 6: the three saved cases, the analyzed pear trials, and the two # treatments of g_V. set_labels <- c(value = "Case 1", associability = "Case 2", reset = "Case 3") process_names <- c(associability = "carried associability", value = "carried learned value", reset = "reset associability") view_labels <- c(late = "pear trials 8–10", early = "pear trials 1–6", full = "all ten pear trials") policy_label <- c(estimated = paste0(gV, " estimated"), zero = paste0(gV, " fixed at zero")) # What the decision rule of Section 6.3 gave, worded to follow "the comparison". decision_text <- c(carry = "favors associability carryover", no_carry = "favors a candidate without associability carryover", unresolved = "is unresolved") # TRUE when the held-out scores of the carryover and reset candidates differ by # less than .01, with a standard error below .01. near_reset_scores <- function(scores) { r <- scores[scores$against == "reset", , drop = FALSE] nrow(r) == 1L && isTRUE(abs(r$difference) < .01 && r$se < .01) }

With a model of simple decisions, we can examine a case in which two parameter settings predict exactly the same probability of a correct response."), h3("Two settings with the same accuracy"), p("Suppose participants judge whether a patch of moving dots is drifting to the left or to the right, and we record only whether each response is correct. The drift diffusion model describes such a decision as the accumulation of noisy evidence until the evidence reaches one of two boundaries. Because the evidence fluctuates from moment to moment, either boundary can be reached on a given trial."), P("The drift rate, v, is how quickly the evidence moves, on average, toward the boundary for the correct response. The boundary separation, a, is the distance between the two boundaries. The farther apart they are, the more evidence must accumulate before a response. Evidence starts halfway between them."), P("Consider two settings. In the first, evidence accumulates slowly, with v = 0.30, and the boundaries are far apart, with a = 2.0. Download a copy to look back over your reasoning. Reopen an earlier step to review a result, or start again to try different answers."), p(actionLink("restart", "Start the inquiry again"), span(class = "muted", " (your notes are kept)")))), last = TRUE ) measurement_server <- function(input, output, answers, add_note) { # The two settings, with their predicted accuracy. output$ddm_table <- renderUI(tags$table(class = "values", tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th(""), tags$th(HTML("Drift rate v")), tags$th(HTML("Boundary separation a")), tags$th("Predicted accuracy"))), tags$tbody( tags$tr(tags$td("First setting"), tags$td(num0(dd$v[1], 2)), tags$td(num0(dd$a[1], 1)), tags$td(num(dd$acc[1]))), tags$tr(tags$td("Second setting"), tags$td(num0(dd$v[2], 2)), tags$td(num0(dd$a[2], 1)), tags$td(num(dd$acc[2])))))) acc_text <- paste0("A correct response is more likely when evidence accumulates faster or when the boundaries are farther apart. content:
# Learning models of Sections 2-4: Rescorla-Wagner (Equation 1) and the
# adaptive model (Equations 2 and 3), and the response functions of Section 5.
# Base R only. The analyses, tests/verify_models.R, the reference
# implementation in R/inference.R and the companion app use these functions.
#
# A design is a list of trials made by make_trials(). Each trial gives the cues
# present ($cues), the outcome lambda ($lambda, 1 or 0) and a phase label
# ($phase).


# Rescorla-Wagner model (Equation 1). The cues present on a trial share one
# prediction error, lambda minus their summed value, and each adds its
# learning rate times this error to its value. beta holds the learning rates,
# one named value per cue, and they do not change with training. Absent cues
# keep their values. Returns one row per cue and trial, holding the value at
# the start of the trial; trial length(design) + 1 holds the values after the
# last trial.
rw_simulate <- function(design, beta, V_init = NULL, cue_names = NULL) {
  if (is.null(cue_names))
    cue_names <- unique(unlist(lapply(design, function(x) x$cues)))
  n_cues   <- length(cue_names)
  n_trials <- length(design)

  if (!all(cue_names %in% names(beta)))
    stop("beta must contain named values for all cues: ", paste(cue_names, collapse = ", "))

  V <- if (is.null(V_init)) setNames(rep(0, n_cues), cue_names) else V_init
  # Column t holds the values at the start of trial t.
  V_by_trial <- matrix(NA_real_, n_cues, n_trials + 1)
  V_by_trial[, 1] <- V[cue_names]

  for (t in seq_along(design)) {
    cues_present <- design[[t]]$cues
    lambda       <- design[[t]]$lambda

    # The error is computed before any value changes, so cues presented
    # together receive the same error (Section 2.2).
    delta <- lambda - sum(V[cues_present])
    V[cues_present] <- V[cues_present] + beta[cues_present] * delta

    V_by_trial[, t + 1] <- V[cue_names]
  }

  phases <- vapply(design, function(x) x$phase, character(1))
  data.frame(
    trial = rep(seq_len(n_trials + 1), each = n_cues),
    phase = rep(c(phases, phases[n_trials]), each = n_cues),
    cue   = rep(cue_names, n_trials + 1),
    V     = as.vector(V_by_trial),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}


# Adaptive model (Equations 2 and 3). Each cue present learns from its own
# error, lambda - V_i, with the learning rate S_i alpha_i: its salience S_i
# times its associability alpha_i. Associability changes by eta times the
# error of the other cues present minus the cue's own error, so it rises when
# the cue predicts more accurately than the other cues, falls when it predicts
# less accurately, and stays unchanged when the errors are equal. A cue
# presented alone is compared with the error of predicting zero, |lambda|.
# Absent cues keep their values and associabilities.
#
# alpha_init and V_init give the state at the start of the run: alpha_init
# and zero before training, or alpha_i(0) (Equation 4) and V_i(0) (Equation 5)
# for a run of pear trials. Associability is kept within
# [alpha_min, alpha_max] = [.01, 1]. Returns one row per cue and trial, holding
# V and alpha at the start of the trial; trial length(design) + 1 holds the
# values after the last trial.
adaptive_simulate <- function(design, S, alpha_init,
                              eta = 0.05,
                              V_init = NULL, cue_names = NULL,
                              alpha_min = 0.01, alpha_max = 1.0) {
  if (is.null(cue_names))
    cue_names <- unique(unlist(lapply(design, function(x) x$cues)))
  n_cues   <- length(cue_names)
  n_trials <- length(design)

  if (!all(cue_names %in% names(S)) || !all(cue_names %in% names(alpha_init)))
    stop("S and alpha_init must contain named values for all cues: ",
         paste(cue_names, collapse = ", "))

  V <- if (is.null(V_init)) setNames(rep(0, n_cues), cue_names) else V_init
  alpha <- alpha_init
  # Column t holds the values and associabilities at the start of trial t.
  V_by_trial <- alpha_by_trial <- matrix(NA_real_, n_cues, n_trials + 1)
  V_by_trial[, 1] <- V[cue_names]
  alpha_by_trial[, 1] <- alpha[cue_names]

  for (t in seq_along(design)) {
    cues_present <- design[[t]]$cues
    lambda       <- design[[t]]$lambda

    # Both the value update and the error comparison use the values at the
    # start of the trial, so a change in associability takes effect on the
    # next trial (Section 3.3).
    V_start <- V

    for (cue in cues_present) {
      V[cue] <- V[cue] + S[cue] * alpha[cue] * (lambda - V[cue])
    }

    # e_own and e_other are e_i and e_-i of Equation 3: the size of the cue's
    # own error and of the error of the other cues' summed prediction.
    for (cue in cues_present) {
      others  <- setdiff(cues_present, cue)
      e_own   <- abs(lambda - V_start[cue])
      e_other <- if (length(others) > 0) {
        abs(lambda - sum(V_start[others]))
      } else {
        abs(lambda)
      }

      alpha[cue] <- max(alpha_min, min(alpha_max, alpha[cue] + eta * (e_other - e_own)))
    }

    V_by_trial[, t + 1] <- V[cue_names]
    alpha_by_trial[, t + 1] <- alpha[cue_names]
  }

  phases <- vapply(design, function(x) x$phase, character(1))
  data.frame(
    trial = rep(seq_len(n_trials + 1), each = n_cues),
    phase = rep(c(phases, phases[n_trials]), each = n_cues),
    cue   = rep(cue_names, n_trials + 1),
    V     = as.vector(V_by_trial),
    alpha = as.vector(alpha_by_trial),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}


# The same two models, returning only the state after the last trial: the
# values, and for the adaptive model also the associabilities. Their loops are
# the ones printed in Sections 2.3 and 3.3. They are written separately from
# rw_simulate() and adaptive_simulate() so that tests/verify_models.R can
# compare the two versions (Section 2.3).
rw_final <- function(design, beta, V_init = NULL) {
  cue_names <- unique(unlist(lapply(design, function(x) x$cues)))
  V <- if (is.null(V_init)) setNames(rep(0, length(cue_names)), cue_names) else V_init
  for (t in seq_along(design)) {
    cues  <- design[[t]]$cues
    delta <- design[[t]]$lambda - sum(V[cues])
    V[cues] <- V[cues] + beta[cues] * delta
  }
  V
}

adaptive_final_state <- function(design, S, alpha_init, eta = 0.05, V_init = NULL) {
  cue_names <- unique(unlist(lapply(design, function(x) x$cues)))
  V <- if (is.null(V_init)) setNames(rep(0, length(cue_names)), cue_names) else V_init
  alpha <- alpha_init
  for (t in seq_along(design)) {
    cues    <- design[[t]]$cues
    lambda  <- design[[t]]$lambda
    e_own   <- abs(lambda - V[cues])
    e_other <- abs(lambda - (sum(V[cues]) - V[cues]))
    V[cues] <- V[cues] + S[cues] * alpha[cues] * (lambda - V[cues])
    alpha[cues] <- alpha[cues] + eta * (e_other - e_own)
    alpha[cues] <- pmin(1, pmax(.01, alpha[cues]))
  }
  list(V = V, alpha = alpha)
}


# n identical trials: the cues present, the outcome lambda and a phase label.
make_trials <- function(cues, lambda, n, phase_label) {
  lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    list(cues = cues, lambda = lambda, phase = phase_label)
  })
}

# Values and associabilities after the last trial of a run of rw_simulate()
# or adaptive_simulate().
extract_final_V <- function(run) {
  final <- run[run$trial == max(run$trial), ]
  setNames(final$V, final$cue)
}

extract_final_alpha <- function(run) {
  final <- run[run$trial == max(run$trial), ]
  setNames(final$alpha, final$cue)
}


# Response functions of Section 5.2, which turn a learned value V into the
# probability of a yes response: the sigmoid of Equation 7, with slope gamma
# and midpoint theta, and the threshold rule, which gives a yes response when
# V exceeds theta and a no response otherwise.
obs_sigmoid <- function(V, gamma = 8, theta = 0.5) {
  1 / (1 + exp(-gamma * (V - theta)))
}

obs_threshold <- function(V, theta = 0.5) {
  as.numeric(V > theta)
}


# Prints the first n_trace trials of a Rescorla-Wagner run step by step, so
# that the calculations of Section 2.2 can be followed by hand. Returns the
# values after those trials.
rw_hand_trace <- function(design, beta, n_trace = 5) {
  cue_names <- unique(unlist(lapply(design, function(x) x$cues)))
  V <- setNames(rep(0, length(cue_names)), cue_names)
  # Numbers as the paper writes them, without a leading zero.
  fmt <- function(x, digits = 4) sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits))

  for (t in seq_len(min(n_trace, length(design)))) {
    cues   <- design[[t]]$cues
    lambda <- design[[t]]$lambda
    phase  <- design[[t]]$phase
    sum_V  <- sum(V[cues])
    delta  <- lambda - sum_V

    cat(sprintf("Trial %d [%s]: cues = {%s}, lambda = %g\n",
                t, phase, paste(cues, collapse = ", "), lambda))
    cat(sprintf("  V before: %s\n",
                paste(sprintf("%s = %s", cue_names, fmt(V[cue_names])), collapse = ", ")))
    cat(sprintf("  delta = lambda - sum of V present = %g - %s = %s\n",
                lambda, fmt(sum_V), fmt(delta)))
    for (cue in cues) {
      cat(sprintf("  change in V_%s = beta_%s * delta = %s * %s = %s\n",
                  cue, cue, fmt(beta[cue], 2), fmt(delta), fmt(beta[cue] * delta)))
    }

    V[cues] <- V[cues] + beta[cues] * delta

    cat(sprintf("  V after:  %s\n\n",
                paste(sprintf("%s = %s", cue_names, fmt(V[cue_names])), collapse = ", ")))
  }
  invisible(V)
}
