# Plots for the companion app

library(ggplot2)

# The colors of the paper's figures (R/figure_style.R), repeated here because
# shiny_app/ is self-contained. B is red and D blue; the two counterbalancing
# groups take the colors of Figure 7a.
ink   <- "#252525"
grey  <- "#696969"
light <- "#BFBFBF"
tint  <- "#EDEDED"
col_B <- "#B64B41"
col_D <- "#35658D"
col_groups <- c(`1` = "#3A8F6A", `-1` = "#5B4B8A")

theme_app <- function(base_size = 13) {
  theme_classic(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      text = element_text(colour = ink),
      axis.text = element_text(colour = ink, size = base_size - 2),
      axis.line = element_line(linewidth = .3, colour = ink),
      axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = .3, colour = ink),
      plot.title = element_text(size = base_size, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 4)),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = base_size - 2, colour = grey, margin = margin(b = 8)),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      strip.background = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(size = base_size - 1, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
      strip.clip = "off",
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.margin = margin(8, 14, 8, 8)
    )
}

# Positions for the labels at the ends of the lines: at least min_gap apart, in
# the order of y, with the same mean as y.
spread_labels <- function(y, min_gap) {
  o <- order(y)
  s <- y[o]
  for (i in seq_along(s)[-1]) s[i] <- max(s[i], s[i - 1] + min_gap)
  y[o] <- s - (mean(s) - mean(y[o]))
  y
}

# A zero line that stops at x_max, so that it does not run through the end labels.
zero_line <- function(x_max, x_min = -Inf)
  annotate("segment", x = x_min, xend = x_max, y = 0, yend = 0, colour = light, linewidth = .3)


# Step 1: the tone and the light under Rescorla-Wagner, as in Figure 2a. Values
# after each completed trial; the gray dashed curve is a new cue trained alone
# over the compound trials, and the dotted line the light's limit.
plot_blocking_values <- function(tr) {
  n <- nrow(tr)
  n1 <- sum(!tr$light)
  d <- rbind(data.frame(cue = "A", t = 0:n, V = c(tr$V_A[1], tr$V_A_after)),
             data.frame(cue = "B", t = 0:n, V = c(tr$V_B[1], tr$V_B_after)))
  alone <- data.frame(t = n1:n, V = 1 - (1 - default_settings$beta)^(0:(n - n1)))
  limit <- (1 - tr$V_A_after[n1]) / 2
  ends <- data.frame(label = c("A (tone)", "B (light)", "new cue alone"),
                     y = c(tail(d$V[d$cue == "A"], 1), tail(d$V[d$cue == "B"], 1), tail(alone$V, 1)),
                     col = c(ink, col_B, grey))
  ends$y <- spread_labels(ends$y, .09)
  ggplot(d, aes(t, V)) +
    annotate("segment", x = n1, xend = n1, y = 0, yend = 1, colour = light, linewidth = .3,
             linetype = "longdash") +
    annotate("text", x = n1 / 2, y = 1.07, label = "A+", size = 3.8, colour = grey) +
    annotate("text", x = n1 + (n - n1) / 2, y = 1.07, label = "AB+", size = 3.8, colour = grey) +
    geom_line(data = alone, colour = grey, linetype = "22", linewidth = .6) +
    annotate("segment", x = n1, xend = n, y = limit, yend = limit, colour = col_B,
             linewidth = .4, linetype = "dotted") +
    geom_line(aes(colour = cue), linewidth = .8) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = cue), size = 1.3) +
    geom_text(data = ends, aes(x = n + .6, y = y, label = label), colour = ends$col, hjust = 0,
              size = 3.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(A = ink, B = col_B)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 5, 10, 15, 20), expand = expansion(mult = c(.01, .02))) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, .5, 1), labels = c("0", ".5", "1")) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, n + 5.5), ylim = c(0, 1.1), clip = "off") +
    labs(x = "Completed trials", y = "Learned value",
         title = "Learned values after each trial",
         subtitle = paste0("Dashed line: the start of the compound trials. Dotted line: B's limit, ",
                           num(limit, 4))) +
    theme_app()
}

# Step 1: the shared error on each trial, as in Figure 2b, with the first
# compound trial circled and, if given, the trial chosen in the table marked.
plot_shared_error <- function(tr, mark = NULL) {
  n1 <- sum(!tr$light)
  p <- ggplot(tr, aes(trial, error)) +
    annotate("segment", x = n1 + .5, xend = n1 + .5, y = 0, yend = 1, colour = light,
             linewidth = .3, linetype = "longdash") +
    geom_line(colour = ink, linewidth = .6) +
    geom_point(colour = ink, size = 1.4) +
    geom_point(data = tr[n1 + 1, ], shape = 21, size = 3, fill = "white", colour = ink, stroke = .7)
  if (!is.null(mark)) p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = mark, colour = grey, linewidth = .4,
                                          linetype = "dotted")
  p + scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 5, 10, 15, 20)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, .5, 1), labels = c("0", ".5", "1")) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = "Trial", y = "Shared error", title = "The shared error on each trial",
         subtitle = paste0("Dashed line: the start of the compound trials. Open circle: trial ",
                           n1 + 1, if (!is.null(mark)) paste0(". Dotted line: trial ", mark))) +
    theme_app()
}


# B and D learning curves, one panel per model, as in Figure 3b and c.
plot_curves <- function(r, labels = c(rw = "Rescorla–Wagner", adaptive = "Adaptive model"),
                        xlab = "Completed pear trials", ylab = "Learned value for the pear") {
  models <- c("rw", "adaptive")
  d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(models, function(m) rbind(
    data.frame(model = labels[[m]], cue = "B", k = r[[m]]$B$k, V = r[[m]]$B$V),
    data.frame(model = labels[[m]], cue = "D", k = r[[m]]$D$k, V = r[[m]]$D$V))))
  d$model <- factor(d$model, levels = unname(labels[models]))
  # When B and D coincide, draw D dashed over B and label the pair once.
  same <- vapply(models, function(m) max(abs(r[[m]]$B$V - r[[m]]$D$V)) < 1e-12, logical(1))
  same_labels <- unname(labels[models][same])
  d$dash <- d$cue == "D" & d$model %in% same_labels
  ends <- d[d$k == max(d$k) & !(d$cue == "B" & d$model %in% same_labels), ]
  ends$label <- ifelse(ends$model %in% same_labels, "B, D", ends$cue)
  ends$col <- ifelse(ends$model %in% same_labels, ink, c(B = col_B, D = col_D)[ends$cue])
  ends$y <- ave(ends$V, ends$model, FUN = function(v) spread_labels(v, .07))
  ggplot(d, aes(k, V, colour = cue)) +
    geom_line(aes(linetype = dash), linewidth = .8) +
    geom_point(size = 1.6) +
    geom_text(data = ends, aes(y = y, label = label), colour = ends$col, hjust = -.25,
              size = 4.2, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "solid", `TRUE` = "22")) +
    facet_wrap(~model, nrow = 1) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(B = col_B, D = col_D)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 5, 10), expand = expansion(mult = c(.02, .16))) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, .5, 1), labels = c("0", ".5", "1")) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1), clip = "off") +   # end labels may run past the panel
    labs(x = xlab, y = ylab) +
    theme_app() +
    theme(panel.spacing.x = unit(1.6, "lines"))
}

# The B-D gap, D minus B, for both models, as in Figure 3d. "ref" adds the
# unchanged adaptive model as a light line, for comparison with a changed one.
plot_gap <- function(r, title = "The B–D gap (D minus B)", ylim = NULL,
                     second = "Adaptive model", ref = NULL, ref_label = "Unchanged",
                     xlab = "Completed pear trials") {
  d <- rbind(data.frame(model = "Rescorla–Wagner", k = r$rw$B$k, gap = r$rw$gap),
             data.frame(model = second, k = r$adaptive$B$k, gap = r$adaptive$gap))
  d$model <- factor(d$model, levels = c("Rescorla–Wagner", second))
  ends <- data.frame(label = c("Rescorla–Wagner", second), gap = d$gap[d$k == max(d$k)],
                     col = c(grey, ink))
  if (!is.null(ref)) {
    ref_gap <- data.frame(k = ref$adaptive$B$k, gap = ref$adaptive$gap)
    ends <- rbind(ends, data.frame(label = ref_label, gap = ref_gap$gap[nrow(ref_gap)],
                                   col = grey))
  }
  y_range <- if (is.null(ylim)) range(d$gap, ends$gap, 0) else ylim
  ends$y <- spread_labels(ends$gap, .075 * diff(y_range))
  k_max <- max(d$k)
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(k, gap)) + zero_line(k_max)
  if (!is.null(ref)) p <- p + geom_line(data = ref_gap, colour = light, linewidth = .8)
  p +
    geom_line(aes(linetype = model, colour = model), linewidth = .8) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = model), size = 1.6) +
    geom_text(data = ends, aes(k_max, y, label = label), colour = ends$col, hjust = 0,
              nudge_x = .03 * k_max, size = 3.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c(grey, ink), c("Rescorla–Wagner", second))) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = setNames(c("22", "solid"), c("Rescorla–Wagner", second))) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, k_max, by = 5), expand = expansion(mult = c(.02, .02))) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = axis_num) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1.55 * k_max), ylim = ylim, clip = "off") +
    labs(x = xlab, y = "Gap in learned value", title = title) +
    theme_app()
}

# Step 3: the adaptive model's gap under several runs, drawn over k_max pear
# trials, with the trials beyond the task's ten shaded, as in Figure 4b. gaps is
# a named list of gap vectors for k = 0, ..., k_max; the first is drawn in ink,
# the others in gray with their own line types.
plot_gap_runs <- function(gaps, title, shade_after = NULL, ylim = NULL,
                          xlab = "Completed pear trials", mark_peak = FALSE, subtitle = NULL) {
  k_max <- length(gaps[[1]]) - 1
  d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(gaps), function(nm)
    data.frame(run = nm, k = 0:k_max, gap = gaps[[nm]])))
  d$run <- factor(d$run, levels = names(gaps))
  types <- setNames(c("solid", "22", "42", "12", "1343")[seq_along(gaps)], names(gaps))
  cols <- setNames(c(ink, rep(grey, length(gaps) - 1)), names(gaps))
  ends <- data.frame(label = names(gaps), gap = vapply(gaps, function(g) g[k_max + 1], 0),
                     col = unname(cols))
  y_range <- if (is.null(ylim)) range(d$gap, 0) else ylim
  ends$y <- spread_labels(ends$gap, .08 * diff(y_range))
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(k, gap))
  if (!is.null(shade_after)) p <- p + annotate("rect", xmin = shade_after, xmax = k_max,
                                               ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = tint)
  p <- p + zero_line(k_max) +
    geom_line(aes(colour = run, linetype = run), linewidth = .8)
  if (mark_peak) {
    top <- d[d$run == names(gaps)[1], ]
    top <- top[which.max(top$gap), ]
    p <- p + geom_point(data = top, shape = 21, size = 3, fill = "white", colour = ink, stroke = .7)
  }
  p + geom_text(data = ends, aes(k_max, y, label = label), colour = ends$col, hjust = 0,
                nudge_x = .03 * k_max, size = 3.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = types) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, k_max, by = 5), expand = expansion(mult = c(.02, .02))) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = axis_num) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1.5 * k_max), ylim = ylim, clip = "off") +
    labs(x = xlab, y = "B–D gap in learned value", title = title, subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_app()
}

# Gap after eight pear trials as the carryover of learned value varies (Figure
# 5a). As in that figure, an open circle marks the adaptive model at g_V = 0,
# and a filled point each model at the value chosen.
plot_gap_by_gV <- function(grid, g_now, cross = NULL) {
  d <- rbind(data.frame(model = "Rescorla–Wagner", g_V = grid$g_V, gap = grid$rw),
             data.frame(model = "Adaptive model", g_V = grid$g_V, gap = grid$adaptive))
  origin <- d$model == "Adaptive model" & d$g_V == 0
  now <- d[abs(d$g_V - g_now) < 1e-9, ]
  ends <- d[d$g_V == max(d$g_V), ]
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(g_V, gap, colour = model, linetype = model)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .8) +
    geom_point(data = d[origin, ], shape = 21, fill = "white", size = 2.6, stroke = .8) +
    geom_point(data = now, size = 3) +
    geom_text(data = ends, aes(label = model), hjust = 0, nudge_x = .02, size = 3.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("Rescorla–Wagner" = grey, "Adaptive model" = ink)) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Rescorla–Wagner" = "22", "Adaptive model" = "solid")) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, .5, 1), labels = c("0", ".5", "1")) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = axis_num) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1.45), ylim = c(0, .32), clip = "off") +
    labs(x = expression("Carryover of learned value, " * italic(g)[V]),
         y = "Gap after eight pear trials",
         title = "The gap after eight pear trials as more value carries over",
         subtitle = "Open circle: the adaptive model without value carryover, as in Step 2. Filled points: your value") +
    theme_app() +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(8, 24, 8, 8))
  if (!is.null(cross)) p <- p +
    annotate("segment", x = cross, xend = cross, y = 0,
             yend = grid$rw[which.min(abs(grid$g_V - cross))], colour = light, linewidth = .4) +
    annotate("text", x = cross, y = .02, label = paste("equal gaps at", num(cross)),
             hjust = 1.06, size = 3.5, colour = grey)
  p
}

# Step 4: the two response functions, as in Figure 6a; with points = TRUE, also
# B's and D's learned values before the responses on pear trials 1, 6 and 10.
plot_response_functions <- function(resp, ks = c(0, 5, 9), points = TRUE) {
  V <- seq(0, 1, by = .005)
  curves <- rbind(data.frame(rule = "Sigmoid", V = V, p = response_prob(V, "sigmoid")),
                  data.frame(rule = "Threshold", V = V, p = response_prob(V, "threshold")))
  marks <- resp[resp$k %in% ks, ]
  pts <- rbind(data.frame(cue = "B", k = marks$k, V = marks$V_B, p = marks$p_B),
               data.frame(cue = "D", k = marks$k, V = marks$V_D, p = marks$p_D))
  pts <- pts[!(pts$k == 0 & pts$cue == "D"), ]
  pts$label <- paste0(pts$cue, ", pear trial ", pts$k + 1)
  pts$label[pts$k == 0] <- "B and D, pear trial 1"
  if (!points) pts <- pts[0, ]
  # B's labels sit below and to the right of the points, D's above and to the
  # left; the shared first point is labeled above.
  pts$hjust <- ifelse(pts$k == 0, -.1, ifelse(pts$cue == "B", -.15, 1.15))
  pts$vjust <- ifelse(pts$k == 0, -1, ifelse(pts$cue == "B", 1.4, -.6))
  marked <- if (nrow(pts)) list(
    geom_point(data = pts, aes(colour = cue), size = 2.4),
    geom_text(data = pts, aes(label = label, colour = cue, hjust = hjust, vjust = vjust), size = 3.4),
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(B = col_B, D = col_D)))
  ggplot(curves, aes(V, p)) +
    geom_line(aes(linetype = rule), colour = ink, linewidth = .7) +
    marked +
    annotate("text", x = .98, y = .9, label = "threshold", hjust = 1, size = 3.4, colour = grey) +
    annotate("text", x = .7, y = .62, label = "sigmoid", hjust = 0, size = 3.4, colour = grey) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(Sigmoid = "solid", Threshold = "22")) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, .5, 1), labels = c("0", ".5", "1")) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, .5, 1), labels = c("0", ".5", "1")) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), clip = "off") +
    labs(x = "Learned value for the pear", y = "Probability of a yes",
         title = "Two response functions",
         subtitle = if (points) "Points: B's and D's learned values before the responses on pear trials 1, 6 and 10") +
    theme_app()
}

# Step 4: D minus B before each of the ten responses, as in Figure 6b: the gap
# in learned values (dashed), the difference in yes probabilities under the
# sigmoid (solid), and, shaded, the responses on which the threshold rule
# predicts different responses. "mark" adds a dotted line at a response.
plot_response_differences <- function(resp, mark = NULL) {
  d <- rbind(data.frame(what = "Gap in learned value", q = resp$k + 1, y = resp$V_D - resp$V_B),
             data.frame(what = "Difference in yes probability, sigmoid", q = resp$k + 1,
                        y = resp$p_D - resp$p_B))
  band <- range(resp$k[resp$t_D != resp$t_B]) + 1
  ends <- d[d$q == 10, ]
  ends$y <- spread_labels(ends$y, .06)
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(q, y)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = band[1] - .5, xmax = band[2] + .5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = tint) +
    annotate("text", x = mean(band), y = .62, label = "threshold rule:\nresponses differ",
             size = 3.3, colour = grey, lineheight = .9) +
    zero_line(10, 1) +
    geom_line(aes(linetype = what), colour = ink, linewidth = .8) +
    geom_point(colour = ink, size = 1.5)
  if (!is.null(mark)) p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = mark, colour = grey, linewidth = .4,
                                          linetype = "dotted")
  p + geom_text(data = ends, aes(x = 10.3, y = y, label = c("gap in\nlearned value",
                                                             "difference in yes\nprobability")[match(what, unique(d$what))]),
                hjust = 0, size = 3.4, colour = ink, lineheight = .9) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Gap in learned value" = "22",
                                     "Difference in yes probability, sigmoid" = "solid")) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, .25, .5), labels = c("0", ".25", ".5")) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1, 12.6), ylim = c(-.02, .66), clip = "off") +
    labs(x = "Response on pear trial", y = "D minus B",
         title = "Differences between D and B before each response",
         subtitle = "Shaded: the responses on which the threshold rule predicts different answers") +
    theme_app()
}

# Step 5: responses of the first 24 participants in a case. Pear trials outside
# cols were not analyzed.
plot_records <- function(case, cols = 1:10, rows = 1:24) {
  y <- case$y[rows, , drop = FALSE]
  d <- expand.grid(participant = seq_along(rows), col = 1:20)
  d$yes <- as.vector(y)
  d$cue <- ifelse(d$col <= 10, "B", "D")
  d$trial <- ifelse(d$col <= 10, d$col, d$col - 10)
  d$fill <- ifelse(!(d$trial %in% cols), "blank", ifelse(d$yes == 1, d$cue, "no"))
  ggplot(d, aes(trial, participant)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = fill), colour = "white", linewidth = .6) +
    facet_wrap(~cue, nrow = 1, labeller = as_labeller(c(B = "Responses to B", D = "Responses to D"))) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(no = "#C9C9C9", B = col_B, D = col_D, blank = "#FAFAFA")) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 5, 10), expand = expansion(0)) +
    scale_y_reverse(breaks = NULL, expand = expansion(0)) +
    labs(x = "Pear trial", y = paste0("Participants 1–", length(rows)),
         subtitle = "Colored: yes · Gray: no · Blank: not analyzed") +
    theme_app() +
    theme(axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
}

# Step 5: each participant's proportion of yes responses to D minus that to B,
# over the analyzed pear trials.
participant_differences <- function(case, cols) {
  y <- case$y
  data.frame(participant = seq_len(nrow(y)), group = case$allocation,
             difference = rowMeans(y[, 10 + cols, drop = FALSE]) - rowMeans(y[, cols, drop = FALSE]))
}
# The differences drawn as in Figure 7a: dots stacked by value and colored by
# counterbalancing group, and below them the mean difference with its 95%
# interval.
group_labels <- c(`1` = "Light 1 is B", `-1` = "Light 2 is B")
plot_participants <- function(case, design) {
  d <- participant_differences(case, design$cols)
  d$value <- round(d$difference, 10)
  d <- d[order(d$value, -d$group), ]
  d$stack <- ave(d$value, d$value, FUN = seq_along)
  e <- design$effect
  top <- max(d$stack)
  step <- 1 / length(design$cols)
  ggplot(d, aes(value, stack)) +
    annotate("segment", x = 0, xend = 0, y = -.18 * top, yend = top + 1, colour = light, linewidth = .3) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = factor(group, levels = c("1", "-1"))), size = if (nrow(d) > 80) 1.5 else 2.2) +
    annotate("segment", x = e[["lower"]], xend = e[["upper"]], y = -.1 * top, yend = -.1 * top,
             colour = ink, linewidth = .8) +
    annotate("point", x = e[["estimate"]], y = -.1 * top, shape = 21, fill = "white",
             colour = ink, size = 3, stroke = .8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = col_groups, labels = group_labels, name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = axis_num, breaks = seq(-1, 1, by = .2)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = range(-.4, .8, d$value + c(-step, step))) +
    labs(x = "Proportion of yes responses, D minus B", y = NULL,
         title = paste0("Each participant's difference (", nrow(d), " participants)"),
         subtitle = "Circle and line: the mean difference and its 95% interval") +
    theme_app() +
    theme(axis.line.y = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.justification = "left", legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
}

# Step 5: the observed difference, yes to D minus yes to B, on each analyzed
# pear trial, with 95% intervals. With truth = TRUE it adds the generating
# probability difference as a wide gray line, as the reveal of Step 6 does.
plot_contrast <- function(case, design, truth = FALSE) {
  d <- design$by_trial
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(trial, estimate)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = light, linewidth = .3)
  if (truth) {
    generating <- data.frame(trial = 1:10, difference = case$true_contrast)
    p <- p + geom_line(data = generating, aes(trial, difference), colour = "#D4D4D4",
                       linewidth = 2.4, lineend = "round")
  }
  p + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 0, colour = grey) +
    geom_point(size = 2.2, colour = ink) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10, limits = c(.5, 10.5)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = axis_num) +
    expand_limits(y = c(-.2, .45)) +
    labs(x = "Pear trial", y = "Yes to D minus yes to B",
         subtitle = if (truth)
           "Points: observed, with approximate 95% intervals\nGray line: the generating model's difference in yes probability"
         else "Observed difference on each pear trial, with approximate 95% intervals") +
    theme_app()
}

# Step 5: held-out log score of the carryover candidate minus each alternative,
# with bars two standard errors either side, as in Figure 7c.
plot_scores <- function(scores) {
  d <- scores
  # Keep a common scale for the saved cases, expanding it to include wider intervals.
  score_range <- range(-70, 130, 0, d$difference - 2 * d$se, d$difference + 2 * d$se)
  # ggplot draws the first level at the bottom, so listing reset first puts
  # fixed-rate at the top, as in Figure 7c.
  d$label <- factor(c(fixed = "Carryover minus\nfixed-rate", reset = "Carryover minus\nreset")[d$against],
                    levels = c("Carryover minus\nreset", "Carryover minus\nfixed-rate"))
  ggplot(d, aes(difference, label)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = light, linewidth = .3) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = difference - 2 * se, xmax = difference + 2 * se),
                  width = 0, colour = grey, linewidth = .8, orientation = "y") +
    geom_point(size = 3, colour = ink) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = score_range) +
    labs(x = "Difference in held-out\nlog score", y = NULL,
         subtitle = "Right of 0: carryover predicted better") +
    theme_app() +
    theme(axis.line.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
}

# Explore: the difference in yes probability, D minus B, for both models
# under the chosen response function.
plot_response_models <- function(r, rule, gamma, theta, second = "Adaptive model") {
  first <- "Rescorla–Wagner"
  rows <- lapply(c("rw", "adaptive"), function(m) data.frame(
    model = c(rw = first, adaptive = second)[[m]], q = r[[m]]$B$k + 1,
    difference = response_prob(r[[m]]$D$V, rule, gamma, theta) -
                 response_prob(r[[m]]$B$V, rule, gamma, theta)))
  d <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  d <- d[d$q <= 10, ]   # the response on pear trial q follows q - 1 completed pear trials
  d$model <- factor(d$model, levels = c(first, second))
  ends <- d[d$q == max(d$q), ]
  ylim <- range(-.05, 1.05, d$difference)
  ends$y <- spread_labels(ends$difference, .075 * diff(ylim))
  ggplot(d, aes(q, difference, colour = model, linetype = model)) +
    zero_line(max(d$q)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .8) +
    geom_point(size = 1.6) +
    geom_text(data = ends, aes(y = y, label = model), hjust = 0, nudge_x = .3, size = 3.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c(grey, ink), c(first, second))) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = setNames(c("22", "solid"), c(first, second))) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 5, 10), expand = expansion(mult = c(.02, .02))) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = axis_num) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1, 15.5), ylim = ylim, clip = "off") +
    labs(x = "Response (pear trial)", y = "Yes probability, D minus B",
         title = "Difference in yes probability under the chosen function") +
    theme_app()
}

# Step 7: the percentage of decisions finished by each time, both boundaries
# together, as in Figure 10c. Dashed lines mark the means and points the
# percentages finished by time 0.5.
plot_ddm_finished <- function(d = ddm_summary()) {
  times <- seq(0, 3.5, by = .0025)
  curves <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), function(i)
    data.frame(id = d$id[i], t = times, p = ddm_finished(times, d$v[i], d$a[i]))))
  at_mean <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), function(i)
    approx(curves$t[curves$id == d$id[i]], curves$p[curves$id == d$id[i]], xout = d$mean[i])$y, 0)
  means <- data.frame(id = d$id, t = d$mean, p = at_mean)
  half <- data.frame(id = d$id, t = .5, p = d$by_half)
  labels <- data.frame(id = d$id, x = c(1.6, .75), y = c(.6, .86),
                       label = c(paste0("First setting: mean ", num0(d$mean[1], 2)),
                                 paste0("Second setting: mean ", num0(d$mean[2], 2))))
  ggplot(curves, aes(t, p, colour = id)) +
    annotate("segment", x = .5, xend = .5, y = 0, yend = 1, colour = light, linewidth = .4,
             linetype = "22") +
    geom_line(linewidth = .8) +
    geom_segment(data = means, aes(x = t, xend = t, y = 0, yend = p), linewidth = .4,
                 linetype = "22") +
    geom_point(data = half, size = 2.4) +
    geom_text(data = half, aes(label = paste0(round(100 * p), "%")), hjust = -.3, vjust = 1.2,
              size = 4, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_text(data = labels, aes(x, y, label = label), hjust = 0, size = 4.2, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(first = ink, second = grey)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, .5, 1, 2, 3), labels = c("0", "0.5", "1", "2", "3"),
                       expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, .5, 1), labels = c("0%", "50%", "100%"),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .03))) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 3.5), ylim = c(0, 1), clip = "off") +
    labs(x = "Decision time (model time units)", y = "Decisions finished",
         title = "Percentage of decisions finished by each time",
         subtitle = "Vertical lines: the mean decision times. Points: decisions finished by time 0.5") +
    theme_app()
}

# Step 1: what one learning rule implies (Section 2)
# The Rescorla-Wagner calculation for the tone and the light, the question of
# the second compound trial (Box 1), the check of the code (Section 2.3), and
# what the comparison with a cue trained alone can show.

rule_ui <- function() {
  scene("scene-1", "1", "What one learning rule implies", "true", "done_q1c",
    "Under Rescorla–Wagner the light ends at .1303, gaining little because the shared error is small. One compound trial with both cues starting at .30 checks the code.",
    h3("Working out the prediction"),
    p("Suppose expectations change when an outcome differs from what was expected. This
       difference is called the prediction error. When the tone and the light appear
       together, each could learn from the error in its own prediction, or both could learn
       from the error in their combined prediction. The Rescorla–Wagner model uses the second.
       It adds the predictions of the signals present and compares their sum with the
       outcome."),
    P("The model keeps a learned value for each signal, also called its associative strength.
       Learned values are quantities calculated within the model, not measurements of a
       participant's expectations. The apple is represented by 1, and both learned values
       start at zero. On a trial followed by the apple, each signal present changes its value
       by a fixed fraction of the prediction error. This fraction is called the learning rate,
       and here it is ", axis_num(default_settings$beta), " for both the tone and the light."),
    P("On the tone's first trial its value is zero, so the error is 1 and the value rises by
       .12 × 1 = .12. On the second trial the error is 1 − .12 = .88, and the value
       rises by .12 × .88 = .1056, to .2256. Each trial leaves 88% of the error, so after
       ten tone-only trials the value is 1 − .88<sup>10</sup> ≈ ",
       num(rw_tr$V_A_after[default_settings$n_first], 4), ". When the light is added, the combined prediction is ",
       num(rw_tr$prediction[11], 4), " + 0, which leaves an error of ", num(rw_tr$error[11], 4),
       ". Both signals learn from this shared error, and each gains .12 × ",
       num(rw_tr$error[11], 4), " ≈ ", num(rw_tr$gain_B[11], 4), ". A new signal trained
       alone would gain .12 on its first trial."),
    p("We write A for the tone and B for the light. Signals such as these are called cues, and a
       trial on which two cues appear together is a compound trial. The training is written
       10 A+ followed by 10 AB+, where the plus sign means that the apple follows."),
    div(class = "scroll-x", tabindex = "0", role = "region",
        `aria-label` = "The first trials, worked by hand", uiOutput("first_trials")),
    rw_formula_ui(),
    div(class = "question", uiOutput("q1a")),
    conditionalPanel("output.done_q1a",
      h3("Checking that the code follows the rule"),
      p("A plausible-looking output can still come from the wrong calculation, so before
         following the remaining trials we check that the program applies the rule. Checking
         that an implementation matches the model's specification is called verification. In
         R, the rule can be written as a short loop:"),
      tags$pre(class = "code", "for (t in seq_along(design)) {
  cues  <- design[[t]]$cues
  delta <- design[[t]]$lambda - sum(V[cues])
  V[cues] <- V[cues] + beta[cues] * delta
}"),
      p("V holds the current learned values, beta the learning rates, and design the cues and
         the outcome of each trial. The program calculates the shared error, delta, from the
         combined prediction before either cue changes value. Two mistakes would be easy to
         make: calculating each cue's own error instead of the shared error, or updating the
         tone first and then recalculating the error for the light."),
      div(class = "question", uiOutput("q1b")),
      conditionalPanel("output.done_q1b",
        h3("The second compound trial"),
        uiOutput("q1a_result"),
        fig("p1_values", "330px"),
        fig("p1_error", "260px"),
        tags$details(class = "worked-example",
          tags$summary("Follow the calculation trial by trial"),
          p("Choose a trial to see the values before it, the shared error and each cue's gain."),
          sliderInput("t1_trial", "Trial", min = 1, max = 20, value = 12, step = 1,
                      ticks = FALSE, width = "320px"),
          div(class = "scroll-x", tabindex = "0", role = "region",
              `aria-label` = "One trial in detail", uiOutput("t1_table"))),
        h3("What we can conclude, and what remains open"),
        P("After ten compound trials, the tone has a learned value of about ",
          num(rw_tr$V_A_after[20], 4), " and the light about ", num(rw_tr$V_B_after[20], 4),
          ". Because the two cues gain the same amount on every compound trial, the tone keeps
          the lead of ", num(rw_tr$V_A_after[10], 4), " that it held when the light was
          introduced. Together they remove 24% of the shared error on each compound trial, so
          their combined prediction approaches 1. The light therefore approaches (1 − ",
          num(rw_tr$V_A_after[10], 4), ")/2 ≈ ", num((1 - rw_tr$V_A_after[10]) / 2, 4),
          ", and after ten compound trials it is already within about ",
          num((1 - rw_tr$V_A_after[10]) / 2 - rw_tr$V_B_after[20]), " of this limit. The limit
          holds for continued compound training with the apple and equal fixed learning
          rates."),
        P("When the light is presented alone, the model's prediction is the light's own learned
          value, about ", num(rw_tr$V_B_after[20], 4), ", because the absent tone contributes
          nothing. A learned value of ", num(rw_tr$V_B_after[20], 4), " does not by itself
          imply a 13% probability of a yes response. That requires a further assumption about
          how learned values relate to responses, which Step 4 examines."),
        div(class = "question", uiOutput("q1c")),
        conditionalPanel("output.done_q1c",
          settled("Under Rescorla–Wagner, the light gains little on each compound trial because the
                   shared error is small, and the tone gains exactly as much as the light. After ten
                   compound trials the light has about .1303, close to its limit of .1393. One
                   compound trial with both cues starting at .30, on which the two calculations
                   disagree, shows that the program applies the shared error.",
                  "Whether the light learned less because its companion had been trained
                   beforehand, and whether a different rule could produce the same pattern for a
                   different reason. Step 2 examines both."),
          aside("Section 2, Figure 2 and Box 1."))))
  )
}


rule_server <- function(input, output, answers, add_note) {
  n1 <- default_settings$n_first

  # The first trials, as the text works them out.
  output$first_trials <- renderUI({
    row <- function(t) {
      r <- rw_tr[t, ]
      gain <- if (r$light) paste0(num(r$gain_A, 4), " each") else num(r$gain_A, 4)
      after <- if (r$light) paste0("A ", num(r$V_A_after, 4), ", B ", num(r$V_B_after, 4))
               else paste0("A ", num(r$V_A_after, 4))
      vrow(t, if (r$light) "A and B" else "A", prob(r$prediction, 4), prob(r$error, 4), gain, after)
    }
    tagList(
      p(class = "table-note", "The first trials, each followed by the apple"),
      tags$table(class = "values",
        tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th("Trial"), tags$th("Cues"), tags$th("Combined prediction"),
                           tags$th("Shared error"), tags$th("Gain"), tags$th("Values after"))),
        tags$tbody(row(1), row(2), row(n1), row(n1 + 1))),
      p(class = "table-note", "Values are calculated without rounding and shown to four decimals."))
  })

  # Box 1: the second compound trial. The expectation is saved first; the
  # result is shown after the check of the code.
  dir_choices <- c(more = "More than on its first compound trial.",
                   less = "Less than on its first compound trial.",
                   same = "The same amount.")
  why_choices <- c(
    error = "The tone and the light together now predict more of the apple, so the error they share is smaller.",
    finished = "The tone has finished learning about the apple, so little is left for the light.",
    rate = "The light's learning rate becomes smaller after its first compound trial.",
    left = "The light still has most of the apple left to learn.")
  q1a_items <- list(
    item("dir", paste0("The light gained about ", num(rw_tr$gain_B[n1 + 1], 4), " on its first
      compound trial. When the tone and the light are again followed by the apple, how much will
      the light gain?"), dir_choices),
    item("why", "What is your reason?", why_choices))
  ask_server("q1a", input, output, answers, q1a_items,
    reason = "Which quantities besides the light's value would you follow to check your reason? (optional)",
    button = "Save my expectation",
    feedback = function(a) p("Your expectation is saved in your notes."),
    on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 1", "Your expectation for the second compound trial",
      q1a_items[[1]]$label,
      paste0(dir_choices[[a$dir]], " Reason: ", why_choices[[a$why]],
             if (nzchar(a$reason)) paste0(" Quantities to follow: ", a$reason)),
      settings = first_set(pear = FALSE)))

  # The check of the code (Section 2.3).
  test_choices <- c(
    single = "Train the tone alone for ten trials and check that it reaches .7215.",
    zero = "Run one compound trial with the tone and the light both starting at zero.",
    thirty = "Run one compound trial with the tone and the light both starting at .30.")
  q1b_items <- list(item("test", "Which test would catch a program that calculates each cue's
    own error instead of the shared error?", test_choices))
  check_text <- paste0("With one cue present, a cue's own error is identical to the shared
    error, so the single-cue check cannot catch the mistake. With both cues at zero, the shared
    error and each cue's own error are all 1, so the two calculations agree again. They agree
    whenever the other cues present predict nothing. With both cues at .30, the shared error
    is 1 − (.30 + .30) = .40, so each cue must gain .12 × .40 = ",
    num(checks$thirty$specified[["B"]]), ". A program that used each cue's own error would give
    .12 × (1 − .30) = ", num(checks$thirty$own[["B"]]), ". A program that updated the
    tone first, to .30 + .048 = .348, and then recalculated the error for the light would give
    the light .12 × [1 − (.348 + .30)] = ", num(checks$thirty$one_at_a_time[["B"]], 5),
    ".")
  check_table <- function() {
    # Gains to at most five decimals, without trailing zeros: .048, .04224.
    short <- function(x) axis_num(round(x, 5))
    prog <- function(label, name) vrow(label, num(rw_tr$V_A_after[n1], 4),
      short(checks$zero[[name]][["B"]]), short(checks$thirty[[name]][["B"]]))
    tagList(
      p(class = "table-note", "What each program gives. The first column of numbers is the
        tone's learned value after ten trials alone. The last two columns are the light's gain on
        one compound trial followed by the apple."),
      div(class = "scroll-x", tabindex = "0", role = "region", `aria-label` = "Three programs",
        tags$table(class = "values",
          tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th("Program"), tags$th("Tone after ten trials alone"),
                             tags$th("From 0 and 0"), tags$th("From .30 and .30"))),
          tags$tbody(prog("Shared error, as specified", "specified"),
                     prog("Each cue's own error", "own"),
                     prog("Tone updated first", "one_at_a_time")))))
  }
  ask_server("q1b", input, output, answers, q1b_items, button = "See what each program gives",
    feedback = function(a) tagList(
      if (a$test != "thirty") p(switch(a$test,
        single = "That test checks the tone's training, but it cannot catch this mistake.",
        zero = "That test catches a program that updates the tone first, but it cannot catch a
          program that uses each cue's own error.")),
      check_table(),
      P(check_text),
      p("These starting values were chosen for the check. They are not the result of the earlier
         training. Calculating a separate error for each cue is a legitimate modeling choice,
         and the second model, in Step 2, makes it. In a program for Rescorla–Wagner, however,
         it would be a mistake. Whether the model gives an adequate account of actual learning
         is a different question, usually called validation.")),
    on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 1", "Checking the code", q1b_items[[1]]$label,
      test_choices[[a$test]],
      result = paste0("Light's gain from .30 and .30: ", num(checks$thirty$specified[["B"]]),
        " as specified, ", num(checks$thirty$own[["B"]]), " with each cue's own error, ",
        num(checks$thirty$one_at_a_time[["B"]], 5), " with the tone updated first."),
      settings = "One compound trial followed by the apple, learning rate .12 for both cues"))

  # The result of Box 1, compared with the saved expectation.
  second <- rw_tr[n1 + 2, ]
  result_text <- paste0("On the second compound trial, the tone has ", num(second$V_A, 4),
    " (its ", num(rw_tr$V_A_after[n1], 4), " plus ", num(rw_tr$gain_A[n1 + 1], 4), ") and the
    light ", num(second$V_B, 4), ". Together they predict ", num(second$prediction, 4), ", so
    the shared error is ", num(second$error, 4), ", and the light gains .12 × ",
    num(second$error, 4), " ≈ ", num(second$gain_B, 4), ", less than on its first compound
    trial. On every compound trial both cues gain value, their combined prediction rises, and the
    shared error and the gains become smaller.")
  why_feedback <- c(
    error = "Your reason matches the calculation.",
    finished = paste0("The tone has not finished learning. It gains ", num(second$gain_A, 4),
      " on this trial, exactly as much as the light, because the two cues share the error and
      have equal learning rates."),
    rate = "Under Rescorla–Wagner the learning rate stays at .12. The gain falls because the
      shared error falls.",
    left = "The light does have most of the apple left to learn, but it does not learn from its
      own error. It learns from the error it shares with the tone, and that error is smaller.")
  output$q1a_result <- renderUI({
    req(answers$q1a, answers$q1b)
    a <- answers$q1a
    tagList(
      p(class = "answered-label", "Your expectation"),
      tags$blockquote(HTML(paste0(dir_choices[[a$dir]], " ", why_choices[[a$why]]))),
      P(result_text),
      P(if (a$dir == "less" && a$why == "error") "Your direction and your reason both match."
        else if (a$dir == "less") paste0("The direction is right, but the reason is not. ",
                                         why_feedback[[a$why]])
        else if (a$why == "error") paste0("Your reason is the right one, but it implies that the
          light gains less, not ", if (a$dir == "more") "more" else "the same", ".")
        else paste0("The light gains less, not ", if (a$dir == "more") "more" else "the same",
                    ". ", why_feedback[[a$why]])),
      p("If we followed only the light, we would see its gain fall but not why. We see why when
         we also follow the tone and the shared error."))
  })
  observeEvent(answers$q1b, {
    a <- answers$q1a
    if (is.null(a)) return()
    add_note("Step 1", "The second compound trial", "How much does the light gain on its second
      compound trial?", paste0(dir_choices[[a$dir]], " ", why_choices[[a$why]]),
      result = result_text, settings = first_set(pear = FALSE))

  output$p1_values <- renderPlot({ req(answers$q1b); plot_blocking_values(rw_tr) })
  output$p1_error <- renderPlot({ req(answers$q1b); plot_shared_error(rw_tr, mark = input$t1_trial) })

    req(answers$q1b, input$t1_trial)
    r <- rw_tr[input$t1_trial, ]
    gain <- function(x) if (is.na(x)) "—" else paste0(".12 × ", prob(r$error, 4),
                                                             " = ", num(x, 4))

        both("Combined prediction", if (r$light) paste0(prob(r$V_A, 4), " + ", prob(r$V_B, 4),

        both("Shared error", paste0("1 − ", prob(r$prediction, 4), " = ", prob(r$error, 4))),

    two = "The light's history differs from that cue's in two ways, so this comparison cannot show which one mattered.",
    any = "Any companion makes a light learn less, whatever the companion's own history.")
  q1c_items <- list(item("show", paste0("The light learned less than a new cue trained alone with
    the apple: about ", num(rw_tr$V_B_after[20], 4), " against ", num(rw_tr$V_A_after[n1], 4),
    " after ten trials. What does this comparison show?"), show_choices))
  q1c_text <- "The light had a companion, and the companion had been trained beforehand. Either
    difference could reduce what the light learns. In the learning literature, blocking is
    defined by a comparison in behavior: responding to a cue is weaker when its companion has
    been trained beforehand than when its companion is new. To find out whether the trained tone
    made the difference, the light has to be compared with a light that also has a companion,
    but a new one."
  ask_server("q1c", input, output, answers, q1c_items,
    feedback = function(a) tagList(
      if (a$show == "tone") p("The comparison changes two things at once, so it cannot single
        out the trained tone.")
      else if (a$show == "any") p("The comparison changes two things at once, so it cannot show

      open = "Did the trained tone make the difference? Could another rule give the same result for a different reason?"))

  # Starting the inquiry again clears the answers but keeps the notes.
  list(reset = function() clear_answers(answers, c("q1a", "q1b", "q1c")))
}

# The model results the page shows, computed once when the app starts. Shiny
# sources the files in R/ in alphabetical order, so this file comes after
# engine.R, which defines the functions used here.

at <- function(x, k) x[k + 1]                # value after k completed pear trials

# Step 1: the trained-tone history under Rescorla-Wagner, and the code check
# of Section 2.3 from starting values of .30 and of zero.
rw_tr   <- rw_trials(default_settings)
checks  <- list(thirty = compound_check(c(A = .3, B = .3)),
                zero = compound_check(c(A = 0, B = 0)))

# Step 2: the two histories under both models, and the pear trials with the
# settings of Section 3.4.
base     <- run_inquiry(default_settings)
trained  <- base$trained

gv1       <- run_inquiry(settings_with(g_V = 1))

  r <- run_inquiry(settings_with(g_V = g))
  r$rw$gap[9] - r$adaptive$gap[9]
}, c(.5, 1), tol = 1e-8)$root

                rank_ties = "Rank-based, ties lower associability")

  list(matched = rule_comparison(rule, 0), mismatched = rule_comparison(rule, 1e-6)))

name: make_inference_cases.R
content:
# Simulated experiments for Steps 5 and 6 of the companion app. In the app, the
# reader designs the experiment: 40 or 160 participants, and the responses on
# pear trials 8-10, on pear trials 1-6, or on all ten pear trials analyzed. For
# each of three generating processes, this script takes one experiment of each
# size from the simulation study, regenerates its responses from the saved
# seed, and analyzes them under each design. The mean D-minus-B difference and
# the held-out comparison of the three candidates, with the carryover of
# learned value estimated and with it fixed at zero, use the study's functions
# in R/inference.R; the first-response check repeats the test of
# analysis/section7_first_response_and_bounds.R. Where the study saved the same
# analysis, the script stops unless the two agree. The study ran the
# comparison with the carryover of learned value fixed at zero only for carried
# associability and carried learned value, with 160 participants and all ten
# pear trials; the other such analyses are made here. Writes
# shiny_app/data/inference_cases.rds.
#   Rscript shiny_app/make_inference_cases.R   (about half a minute)
#
# Selection: for each process, the first experiment of each size in the
# study's base parameter set (config 1). The experiment generated by carried
# learned value with 160 participants is also the first in that parameter set in which
# the restricted comparison favored associability carryover; the app says so
# when it reveals the process, and reports how often that happened across all
# 400 experiments. The study's names for the processes are value (carried
# learned value), associability (carried associability), reset (reset
# associability) and response (lower response intercept for B).

if (!file.exists("R/inference.R")) stop("Run this script from the repository root.")
source("R/inference.R")

study_dir <- "results/section6"
jobs <- read.csv(file.path(study_dir, "jobs.csv"))
generating <- read.csv(file.path(study_dir, "generating_parameters.csv"))
saved <- read.csv(file.path(study_dir, "results.csv"))
study <- read.csv(file.path(study_dir, "summary.csv"))
first_checks <- read.csv(file.path(study_dir, "initial_response_checks.csv"))
first_summary <- read.csv(file.path(study_dir, "initial_response_summary.csv"))

sources <- c("value", "associability", "reset")
sizes <- c(40L, 160L)
views <- c("late", "early", "full")
view_cols <- list(late = 8:10, early = 1:6, full = 1:10)
# The app's names for the two choices of g_V, and the study's.
policies <- c(estimated = "value_allowed", zero = "value_zero")

first_in_config1 <- function(scenario, n) {
  min(saved$id[saved$scenario == scenario & saved$n == n & saved$config == 1 &
                 saved$view == "full" & saved$policy == "value_allowed"])
}
stopifnot(first_in_config1("value", 160) ==
  min(saved$id[saved$scenario == "value" & saved$n == 160 & saved$config == 1 &
                 saved$policy == "value_zero" & saved$decision == "carry"]))

# The first-response check of Section 7.2: the exact one-sided paired test of
# equal first responses to B (column 1) and D (column n_pres + 1). Among the
# participants whose two first responses differ, the number who answer yes to
# D only is binomial with probability .5 under equality.
first_response_check <- function(y, n_pres = 10L) {
  d_only <- sum(y[, n_pres + 1L] == 1 & y[, 1L] == 0)
  b_only <- sum(y[, n_pres + 1L] == 0 & y[, 1L] == 1)
  discordant <- d_only + b_only
  p <- if (discordant == 0) 1 else pbinom(d_only - 1, discordant, .5, lower.tail = FALSE)
  list(d_only = d_only, b_only = b_only, p = p, n = nrow(y))
}

# The D-minus-B difference in yes proportions on each analyzed pear trial q,
# with the interval of Figure 7b (Agresti and Min, 2005): add 1/2 to each cell
# of the paired 2 x 2 table, then use the Wald interval for the difference of
# the two discordant proportions. These are the points and bars of the app's
# plot of the differences by pear trial.
contrast_by_trial <- function(y, cols, n_pres = 10L) {
  n <- nrow(y)
  t(vapply(cols, function(q) {
    n_d_only <- sum(y[, n_pres + q] == 1 & y[, q] == 0)
    n_b_only <- sum(y[, q] == 1 & y[, n_pres + q] == 0)
    p_d <- (n_d_only + .5) / (n + 2)
    p_b <- (n_b_only + .5) / (n + 2)
    se <- sqrt((p_d + p_b - (p_d - p_b)^2) / (n + 2))
    c(trial = q, estimate = (n_d_only - n_b_only) / n,
      lower = p_d - p_b - qnorm(.975) * se, upper = p_d - p_b + qnorm(.975) * se)
  }, numeric(4)))
}

# The carryover candidate's held-out score minus that of each alternative, with
# its standard error.
score_table <- function(comparison) {
  scores <- as.data.frame(comparison$carry_contrasts)
  scores$against <- rownames(scores)
  rownames(scores) <- NULL
  scores[, c("against", "difference", "se")]
}

# The analyses of one design, which use only the analyzed responses. The
# comparisons are returned for the checks against the study and dropped before
# saving.
analyze <- function(observed, view) {
  recorded <- inference_view(observed, view)
  comparisons <- list(estimated = inference_compare(recorded, value = TRUE),
                      zero = inference_compare(recorded, value = FALSE))
  list(cols = view_cols[[view]],
       effect = inference_effect(recorded),
       by_trial = as.data.frame(contrast_by_trial(observed$y, view_cols[[view]])),
       scores = lapply(comparisons, score_table),
       decision = lapply(comparisons, `[[`, "decision"),
       first = if (1L %in% view_cols[[view]]) first_response_check(observed$y) else NULL,
       comparisons = comparisons)
}

cases <- list()
for (src in sources) for (n in sizes) {
  id <- first_in_config1(src, n)
  job <- jobs[jobs$id == id, ]
  setting <- generating[generating$scenario == src & generating$config == job$config, ]
  par <- unlist(setting[inference_names])
  generated <- inference_generate(job$n, par, setting$adaptive, job$seed)
  observed <- generated$observed
  truth_p <- generated$truth$probability

  designs <- lapply(views, function(view) analyze(observed, view))
  names(designs) <- views

  # Agreement with the study, wherever it saved the same analysis.
  for (view in views) for (policy in names(policies)) {
    row <- saved[saved$id == id & saved$view == view & saved$policy == policies[[policy]], ]
    if (!nrow(row)) next
    comparison <- designs[[view]]$comparisons[[policy]]
    effect <- designs[[view]]$effect
    stopifnot(nrow(row) == 1,
              abs(effect[["estimate"]] - row$estimate) < 1e-9,
              abs(effect[["lower"]] - row$lower) < 1e-9, abs(effect[["upper"]] - row$upper) < 1e-9,
              effect[["detected"]] == row$detected,
              abs(comparison$carry_contrasts["fixed", "difference"] - row$carry_vs_fixed) < 5e-5,
              abs(comparison$carry_contrasts["reset", "difference"] - row$carry_vs_reset) < 5e-5,
              identical(comparison$decision, row$decision))
  }
  # The study made the first-response check for every experiment.
  first <- designs$full$first
  saved_first <- first_checks[first_checks$id == id, ]
  stopifnot(first$d_only == saved_first$discordant_control,
            first$b_only == saved_first$discordant_blocked,
            abs(first$p - saved_first$initial_p) < 1e-12)
  for (view in views) designs[[view]]$comparisons <- NULL

  # true_contrast is the generating D-minus-B difference in the probability of a
  # yes on each pear trial, averaged over the participants.
  cases[[src]][[as.character(n)]] <- list(
    id = id, seed = job$seed, n = job$n, source = src, config = job$config,
    generating = as.list(par),
    y = observed$y, allocation = observed$allocation,
    true_contrast = colMeans(truth_p[, 11:20] - truth_p[, 1:10]),
    designs = designs)
  cat(sprintf("%s, %d participants: experiment %d analyzed under %d designs\n",
              src, n, id, length(views)))
}

# Rates across the study's 400 experiments per design with the carryover of
# learned value estimated; for 160 participants and all ten pear trials, also
# the rates of the restricted comparison and those of the first-response check.
rates <- study[study$scenario %in% sources & study$policy == "value_allowed",
               c("scenario", "n", "view", "detected", "carry", "no_carry", "unresolved",
                 "repetitions", "fit_problem")]
rownames(rates) <- NULL
zero_rates <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("associability", "value"), function(src) {
  restricted <- saved[saved$scenario == src & saved$n == 160 & saved$view == "full" &
                        saved$policy == "value_zero", ]
  data.frame(scenario = src, n = 160L, view = "full", repetitions = nrow(restricted),
             carry = mean(restricted$decision == "carry"))
}))
# The first-response check with 160 participants: for carried associability
# and carried learned value, also among the experiments in which the
# restricted comparison favored associability carryover.
first_160 <- first_checks[first_checks$n == 160, ]
first_rates <- merge(first_summary,
  data.frame(scenario = names(tapply(first_160$initial_p < .05, first_160$scenario, mean)),
             rejection_160 = as.vector(tapply(first_160$initial_p < .05, first_160$scenario, mean))),
  all = TRUE)
stopifnot(all(abs(first_rates$initial_rejection - first_rates$rejection_160) < 1e-12,
              na.rm = TRUE))

# The process with a lower response intercept for B (Section 7.3), with 160
# participants and all ten pear trials: candidates with one response function
# for both lights, and candidates that may give B its own response intercept.
# ranked_carry is the share of experiments in which the carryover candidate
# had the highest held-out score, with or without the margin.
response_rates <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("value_allowed", "response_allowed"), function(pol) {
  row <- study[study$scenario == "response" & study$policy == pol, ]
  runs <- saved[saved$scenario == "response" & saved$view == "full" & saved$policy == pol, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(row) == 1, nrow(runs) == row$repetitions,
            abs(mean(runs$decision == "carry") - row$carry) < 1e-12)
  data.frame(policy = pol, repetitions = row$repetitions, detected = row$detected,
             carry = row$carry, no_carry = row$no_carry, unresolved = row$unresolved,
             ranked_carry = mean(runs$winner == "carry"))
}))

saveRDS(list(cases = cases, rates = rates, zero_rates = zero_rates, first_rates = first_rates,
             response_rates = response_rates),
        "shiny_app/data/inference_cases.rds")
cat("Saved shiny_app/data/inference_cases.rds\n")
